Since Agni is produced in this way by the application of force, it is a usage particularly common in the Ṛgveda to call Agni सहसः पुत्रं (*sahasaḥ putraṃ*), the son of strength, that is, one produced by the application of force. On the matter of agni-mathana see what is written in the Special Topics of the 3rd Ṛk of this sūkta (page 37).

To great Agni, great through excess of ability, worthy of sacrifice, the showerer of ṛta (ṛta is water, as it is read among the names of water), the strong (asura means mighty), the showerer of desires, I bring forward an utterance in the form of praise, a means of knowledge, directed to him. How? As ghee, well purified, poured into the mouth at the sacrifice is pleasing to him, so I bring a praise that is pleasing.
- यज्ञे (*yajñe*)—at the time of the sacrifice
- आस्येन (*āsyena*)—as one offers it into the mouth of Agni
- बृहते (*bṛhate*)—to him who has the nature of greatness
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—the causer of rain (the one who pours down rain)
- प्रतीचीं (*pratīcīṃ*)—that which comes to meet him
notes: ಧೃತಂ printed with dh; the Saṃhitā has ಘೃತಂ; read as ghee

en: As, at the time of the sacrifice, a stream of well-purified ghee is offered into the mouth of Agni, so I offer, to Agni, who has the nature of greatness, is worthy of sacrifice, causes rain, is endowed with strength and showers desires, a praise that brings about reflection and comes to meet him.
I offer to the great, the adorable Agni. the rainer of water, the vigorous, the showerer (of benefits), the present acceptable praise, like well-purified butter (poured) at sacrifices into his mouth.

बृहते—सामर्थ्यातिशयेन महते । (*bṛhate—sāmarthyātiśayena mahate |*) The abilities of Agni are many: the power to give the desired objects to those who worship him, the power to destroy enemies, the power to carry the oblations and other materials that the sacrificers offer in him to the gods for whom they are intended, and many other kinds of power and ability. Because Agni has these, he is possessed of excess of ability, and so the great nature of Agni is set out here.
असुराय (*asurāya*)—The word asura has many meanings. Here असुराय—बलवते । (*asurāya—balavate |*) the word is used in the sense of strength.
प्रतीचीं (*pratīcīṃ*)—This word is an adjective of the word गिरं (*giraṃ*). The main purport is: I stand facing Agni and recite the words of praise.

सुपूतं धृतं आस्स्येन (*supūtaṃ dhṛtaṃ āssyena*)—Here an illustration is given for reciting the hymn while standing facing Agni. It is a matter of experience that when ghee (ghṛta) is offered in Agni it burns blazing and shining; that is, the idea is suggested that Agni is pleased by a stream of ghee. Therefore, in the way in which Agni is pleased when ghee is offered in the mouth of Agni, that is, in the Agni blazing with flames, in that way the seer describes: may Agni be pleased with the words of praise that I, the seer, recite standing facing Agni.

ṛta here means praise. O Agni, who know (cikitvaḥ), know this praise made by me. Further, to nourish the world, to bring about the abundant streams of ṛta, that is, of water, pierce (tṛndhi) the clouds. I, endowed with strength, do not touch (sapāmi), that is, I do not practise, the violence that destroys sacrificial rites; and with the two, truth and untruth, I do not do any act that is not Vedic. But I address only praise to you, the radiant one, the showerer of desires.
- अनु त्वंधि (*anu tvaṃdhi*)—cause (from the cloud) to pour down
- यातुं (*yātuṃ*)—the act that obstructs the rite
- न सपामि (*na sapāmi*)—I do not practise
- द्वयेन (*dvayena*)—either by truth or by untruth
- अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*)—of you who have a radiant colour
O Agni, you who know the excellence of my praise, praise this hymn composed by me. Cause streams of water to pour abundantly from the cloud. I, from pride in my strength,
do not practise obstruction of the rite. Either by truth or by untruth, I do not trouble the rite. But I compose and recite praise of you, who have a radiant colour and shower desires.

Agni, who know (the purpose of) the sacrifice, assent to this rite: be favourable to the copious showers of water : (endowed) with strength, (I undertake) not (to obstruct) sacred acts, nor adjure the rite with both (truth and untruth), but (repeat the praise) of the resplendent showerer (of benefits).

The meaning of this Ṛk is not so clear. To make the meaning clear, many words have been supplied, and an effort has been made so that a definite sense becomes evident. Only some of them are explained here.

ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—In this Ṛk this word is read three times. For this word ṛta Sāyaṇa gives the meaning "this hymn made by me (the seer)". For the word ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*) he gives the meaning उदकस्य (*udakasya*), "of the waters". For the use of the word dhārāḥ, "streams of water", in ऋतस्य धाराः (*ṛtasya dhārāḥ*) indicates that the word ṛtasya means water (or ghee?).
यातुं—कर्मणां नाशकरीं हिंसां । (*yātuṃ—karmaṇāṃ nāśakarīṃ hiṃsāṃ |*) He has fitted the meaning: the violence that causes obstruction to the sacrificial rite.
द्वयेन (*dvayena*)—Here also an explanation is given that the two are two kinds of rite, truth and untruth.

O Agni, who make water, the means of life of all beings, by what rite performed with truth do you become the knower of our praise? The praiseworthy one, the guardian of the seasons (the second word for "season" is only a repetition), the shining Agni, may he know me. Of me, the one who serves him, whose wealth consists of cattle and the like, I do not know that Agni, the lord. He explains नवेदाः (*navedāḥ*) as having the sense "he knows" (not "he does not know"), which is obtained by an irregular formation; he adopts the view of Skandasvāmin, while Pāṇini by the sūtra नभ्राण्णपादिति (*nabhrāṇṇapāditi*) gives the word a sense that does not fit here, so that the sense is not suitable. ⟨NOTE:13⟩
notes: ವೇತ್ತೀತ್ಯೇತಸ್ಮಿನ್ನರ್ಥೇ printed for Pāṇini's sense; ನ ವೇತ್ತಿ expected from the context; left as printed

en: - कया ऋतेन (*kayā ṛtena*)—by what rite, of the nature of truth

O Agni, you who provide water to all beings and do good to the world, which of our rites can make you know our praise? May Agni, the praiseworthy one, the guardian of the seasons, the shining one, know me as his devotee. Only Agni, the lord of my wealth, I have not yet seen face to face.

Agni, bestower of water, by what (act of) truth may you, who are adorable, be cognizant of our adoration ? may the divine Agni, the guardian of the seasons recognize me : I (know) him not (yet) as the lord of the riches of which I am the possessor.

In this Ṛk also the word ṛtu is used four times. For the first, ऋतुयन् (*ṛtuyan*), the meaning given is water; for the second, ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), a rite of the nature of truth; for the third and the fourth, the words ऋतूनां ऋतुपाः (*ṛtūnāṃ ṛtupāḥ*), the meaning given is the seasons (words denoting time). Here there is a repetition, ऋतुपा ऋतूनां (*ṛtupā ṛtūnāṃ*). Such repeated expressions are specially found in the Ṛgveda: रयिपतिं रयाणां (*rayipatiṃ rayāṇāṃ*); विशां विश्वतिं (*viśāṃ viśvatiṃ*); रयाणां त्वा रयिपतिं (*rayāṇāṃ tvā rayipatiṃ*); वसूनां वसुपतिं (*vasūnāṃ vasupatiṃ*), and so on.

सनितुः अस्य रायः पतिं अहं न—भजमानस्य मम पश्वादिलक्षणस्य धनस्य स्वामिनं तमग्निं नाहं जानामि । (*sanituḥ asya rāyaḥ patiṃ ahaṃ na—bhajamānasya mama paśvādilakṣaṇasya dhanasya svāminaṃ tamagniṃ nāhaṃ jānāmi |*) Agni is the lord of wealth. This wealth is of many kinds, such as cattle, food and houses. The seer says that he (being of little understanding) does not know well the qualities and surpassing powers of Agni, the lord of such wealth, and thus expresses the greatness of Agni and his own smallness.

O Agni, who are those of your people that would be the binders of one's enemy? By reason of their surpassing power no one can know of what kind such men are: this is the meaning. Who among yours are the radiant protectors of people, who give wealth to the poor? Who of yours protect the man who bears untruth? Who are there as guardians of evil speech, such as a curse? None at all: this is the meaning. Or else: whoever are the binders of the enemy; whoever are the protectors who give wealth and are radiant; whoever protect the man who bears untruth by turning him away from the sin born of untruth and giving him the right path; whoever are guardians of evil speech of the nature of curses and the like: all of these are yours, that is, your worshippers.
- ते (*te*)—among the men who belong to you

O Agni, among the company of men who belong to you, who are the good and who are the bad? How many are there who bind enemies and give wealth to the afflicted, who are radiant and protectors of the poor? How many are there who protect the man of untruthful nature and his evil deeds? Who are they?

Who, Agni, among your (followers) are the imprisoners of foes ? who among them are the protectors (of men), the splendid distributors of gifts ? who among them defend the asserter of untruth ? who are the encouragers of evil deeds ?

O Agni, those who conquer and bind the enemy, the protectors of the poor, those who give wealth to the afflicted, those who protect, without seeing, those who have spoken untruth, ⟨NOTE:14⟩ and those who have gained good sense so as not to speak evil words: all such good men are yours, that is, they are those who worship you. This is the main purport.
notes: ಕಾಣದೆ ಅನೃತವನ್ನಾಡಿದವರನ್ನು: sense of ಕಾಣದೆ unclear

en: O Agni, these friends of yours, your praisers, dispersed and spread everywhere, who were formerly inauspicious, reviling others and the like and abandoning your service, and so unfortunate, have now become auspicious and fortunate, rendering you service. Moreover, those who, to me who conduct myself straight and rightly, speak crooked things with words, that is, with evil speech: these my rivals may themselves be harmed. The word अहिंस्यंत (*ahiṃsyaṃta*) is given as the sense of the verb form.
- एते ते सखायः (*ete te sakhāyaḥ*)—these men, friends of yours
- अशिवाः संतः (*aśivāḥ saṃtaḥ*)—(formerly, not worshipping you) being doers of inauspicious acts; (now)
- शिवासः (*śivāsaḥ*)—in the auspicious work of your worship
- ऋजूयते (*ṛjūyate*)—to me, the doer of good acts
- अधूर्षत (*adhūrṣata*)—let them bring harm upon themselves
O Agni, these men, friends of yours, dispersed and settled everywhere, who formerly, not worshipping you, were doers of inauspicious acts, are now engaged in the auspicious work of your worship.
Let these my enemies, who practise deceitful acts upon me, the doer of good acts, by the use of evil words, bring harm upon themselves of their own accord.

These your friends, Agni, everywhere dispersed, were formerly unhappy (in abandoning your worship), but are again fortunate (by its renewal); may they who, with (censorous) words, impute fraudulent (practices) to me who pursue a straight path, bring evil upon themselves.

Those who are now good men were formerly, that is, before worshipping Agni, wicked and used to do evil deeds. All such wicked people, having worshipped Agni and thereby gained good sense, have become good men. But for all those who have not become good in that way by serving Agni, the wicked people who are my enemies and deceive me, may harm come according to the fruit of their deeds. This is the main purport.

O Agni, the man who praises you, the one worthy of worship, with reverent praise; or else, the man who worships you with the oblation in the form of food, offering the sacrifice to you. (The explanation of the verbal form for this second view is a matter of grammar.) He protects the praise belonging to Agni, the shining one, the showerer of desires. The house of that sacrificer becomes extensive, that is, it becomes full of wealth such as cattle. To the man who goes forth in service of you, may a virtuous remnant, one who accomplishes desires, come: what remains is called the remnant, that is, a son; the meaning is "may he come, may he be".
- अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*)—of the one who has a radiant lustre ⟨NOTE:15⟩
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—of Agni, the showerer of desires
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the praise that is a part of the sacrifice
- आ एतु (*ā etu*)—may he be born
notes: ಅರೋಚಕವಾದ ಕಾಂತಿಯುಳ್ಳವನೂ printed (Bhāvārtha ಆರೋಚಕವಾದ); Sāyaṇa ರೋಚಮಾನಸ್ಯ; read here as "radiant"

en: O Agni, the man who praises you, the one worthy of worship, with reverent praise protects the praise, a part of the sacrifice, of Agni, who is radiant and a showerer of desires. The dwelling-house of that same sacrificer grows extensive. To the man who worships you most excellently, may a son of good understanding be born.

May the dwelling of him, Agni, who celebrates your worship with reverence, of him who protects the sacrifice (offered) to the resplendent showerer (of benefits), be well stored and may a virtuous successor of the man who diligently worships you come in his place.

In the two preceding Ṛks the seer told of the troubles that come to those who do not worship Agni; in this Ṛk he describes the fruit that comes to those who praise Agni and offer oblations. The houses of the good men who, offering oblations to Agni, the one worthy of sacrifice, worship with salutation and praise the shining Agni, the giver of what is desired, will prosper. Prosperity in cattle and the like will come to them. A good and worthy son will be born to them: so the seer has described.

O Agni, we who adore you invoke you. Adoring, that is, praising, we kindle you with fuel-sticks, we make you blaze, for our protection or for your satisfaction. The word अर्चंत (*arcaṃta*) stands a third time for the sake of great respect.
O Agni, worshipping you, we pray and call you for our help. Praising you, we make you blaze for our protection.
Adoring you, Agni, we invoke you: adoring you we kindle you, adoring you for protection.
We who desire wealth recite today, on this day, the praise of the shining Agni, who pervades the sky in the form of the sun: a praise that accomplishes the aims of man.
- दिविस्पृशः (*divispṛśaḥ*)—of him who pervades the intermediate space in the form of the sun
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—the praise that is addressed to Agni
- सिद्धं (*siddhaṃ*)—that accomplishes the aims of man
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice

We who desire wealth recite, at the time of this sacrifice, the praise addressed to the shining Agni, who pervades the intermediate space in the form of the sun, the praise that accomplishes the aims of man.
Desirous of wealth, we recite to-day the effectual praise of the divine Agni, (whose radiance) reaches the sky.

It has been explained many times before that Agni pervades in three forms: in heaven in the form of Āditya, in the intermediate space in the form of lightning-fire, and on earth in the form of terrestrial fire (the sacrificial fire, the household fire or the forest fire). In the present Ṛk it is explained that Agni shines in heaven (the intermediate space) in the form of the sun.

सिद्ध्रं-साधनं । (*siddhraṃ-sādhanaṃ |*) Yāska has explained that the word sidhra has the meaning "means" (Ni. 9-38), and as an example has cited the mantra ⟨NOTE:17⟩ द्यावा नः पृथिवी इमं सिध्रमद्य दिविस्स,शं । यज्ञं देवेषु यच्छतां ॥ (*dyāvā naḥ pṛthivī imaṃ sidhramadya divissa,śaṃ | yajñaṃ deveṣu yacchatāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-41-20).
notes: ಮಕ್ಕಳನ್ನು printed (ಮಂತ್ರವನ್ನು?)

en: The Hotā, the invoker of the gods, who dwells among men: may that Agni accept our praises, that is, partake of them. May that Agni offer sacrifice to the people connected with the gods.
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—words in the form of praise
- दैव्यं जनं (*daivyaṃ janaṃ*)—with reference to people of divine nature
May that Agni who stands in the midst of men partake of our praises, and may he perform the sacrifice with reference to the people of divine nature.
May Agni, who amongst men is the invoker of the gods, accept our praises ; may he offer sacrifice to the divine beings-

यः अग्निः मानुषेषु आ (*yaḥ agniḥ mānuṣeṣu ā*)—the Agni who is among men, that is, the sacrificial fire established on the sacrificial altar in the form of Gārhapatya and the rest. In the preceding Ṛk the Agni who is in heaven in the form of Āditya was praised; in this Ṛk the terrestrial Agni is praised. Although the terrestrial fire has the varieties sacrificial fire, household fire and forest fire, here there is the prayer नः गिरः जुषत (*naḥ giraḥ juṣata*), "may he partake of our praises", and so it should be understood that the praise is addressed to the sacrificial fire alone.
दै व्यं जनं (*dai vyaṃ janaṃ*)—देवसंबंधिनं जनं (*devasaṃbaṃdhinaṃ janaṃ*): people connected with the gods, that is, the gods who are invoked in the sacrifice: such is the purport.

O Agni, you who are ever pleased, who are to be chosen by all, the Hotā, are spread widely everywhere. So Yāska says: सर्वतः पृथुः (*sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*) (Ni. 6. 7.). Moreover, all sacrificers extend the sacrifice by you as the means.
- सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*)—having gained pre-eminence in every way
- वि तन्वते (*vi tanvate*)—(the sacrificers) carry out
O Agni, you who are fully satisfied, honoured by all and the accomplisher of the offering, have gained pre-eminence in every way. By your help alone the sacrificers carry out the sacrifice.
You, Agni, are mighty and gracious, the (ministrant) priest, the desired (of all): through you worshippers complete the sacrifice.
जुष्टः (*juṣṭaḥ*)—सर्वदा प्रीतः (*sarvadā prītaḥ*). The purport is: one who is always pleased, who is delighted, with the oblations and the like that the sacrificers offer in the sacrifice.

वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—सर्वैर्वर्णीयः (*sarvairvarṇīyaḥ*): one who is desired by all. Since a sacrifice cannot be performed without Agni, all people, the sacrificers and the rest, desire Agni; Agni is needed by all. Therefore in the second half of this Ṛk it is said त्वया यज्ञं वि तन्वते (*tvayā yajñaṃ vi tanvate*): all perform the sacrifice by you (with your help).

सप्रथाः (*saprathāḥ*)—सर्वतः पृथुः (*sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*). त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असीत्यपि निगमो भवति (*tvamagne saprathā asītyapi nigamo bhavati*) (Ni. 6-7). Since Agni pervades everywhere (when he burns), he spreads very widely: thus Yāska explained the meaning of the word saprathāḥ and gave this very Ṛk as the example.

O Agni, the wise praisers, the intelligent ones, make you grow with their hymns: you, the giver of food (vāja is food, and you give it), well praised by the great seers of old, thoroughly praised. May you, such as you are, give us excellent strength that is to be praised by all.
O Agni, the wise praisers cause you to grow, you who are the giver of food and are praised by all. May you, such as you are, produce praiseworthy strength for us.
Wise worshippers exalt you, Agni, the bountiful giver of food, the deservedly lauded : bestow upon us excellent strength.

विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—The word vipra is read among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19); it means intelligent people. This word is also used in the sense of the officiating priests who take part in the sacrifice and of the praisers. There is the explanation of Durgācārya: विविधानर्थानस्य प्राप्तुं धातीति विप्रः (*vividhānarthānasya prāptuṃ dhātīti vipraḥ*). Saying that medhāvin means one who possesses intellect, Yāska states the etymology मेधावी कस्मान्मेधया तद्वान् भवति । मेधा मता धीयते । (*medhāvī kasmānmedhayā tadvān bhavati | medhā matā dhīyate |*) (Ni. 3-19). Asking what a medhāvin is, he explains the meaning: the man in whose intellect there is excellent knowledge, a man who possesses such power of intellect.

वाजसातमं सुष्टुतं विप्रा वर्धंति (*vājasātamaṃ suṣṭutaṃ viprā vardhaṃti*)—the people who, praising him with hymns and the like, offer oblations in the sacrifice, this Agni, the giver of food and praised by all, in the sacrifices with fuel and the like
materials, and with oblations of ghee, make to blaze well (to burn brilliantly): such is the purport.

O Agni, you surround the gods, that is, you surpass them by your own brilliance. How? Like the shining outer rim of a wheel, which encloses the spokes fixed in the nave, the fine supports, as it were. Moreover you bring about manifold राधः (*rādhaḥ*), riches: that by which men accomplish their aims is riches. Accomplish them for your praisers. Since the word is read among the names of wealth, it is said that riches means wealth.
- नेमिः (*nemiḥ*)—the outer rim of the wheel
- अरानिव (*arāniva*)—as if encircling all the spokes inside the wheel
O Agni, as the outer rim of a wheel surrounds all the spokes inside the wheel, you surround and pervade all the gods. May you, who have such greatness, fill us, your praisers, with manifold riches.
Agni, you encompass the gods as the circumference (surrounds) the spokes (of a wheel) : bestow manifold wealth upon us.

अग्ने । नेमिः । अरान् इव । देवान् । त्वं । परिभूः । असि । (*agne | nemiḥ | arān iva | devān | tvaṃ | paribhūḥ | asi |*)—As in the wheel of a chariot the outer rim (Rim, or Tyre) surrounds and encloses the spokes (Spokes), Agni stays surrounding all the gods. That is, since he carries the oblation to all the gods, he stays near those gods; the purport is suggested that he goes to all the gods and returns for the carrying of the oblation.

O praiser, awaken Agni, the immortal, who has not the nature of dying, with praise, that is, with a hymn; awaken him thoroughly for the accomplishment of your desired aims. May that Agni, who is well kindled by hymns, that is, shines well, place our oblations among the gods.
- (O praiser) अमूर्त्यं (*amūrtyaṃ*)—who is free from the nature of death
O praiser, awaken with praise Agni, who is free from the nature of death. May Agni, well kindled, take our oblations and place them among the gods.
Waken the immortal Agni with praise, that, being kindled, he may bear our oblations to the gods.

In this Ṛk, the words "awaken Agni, who is free from the nature of death, with praise and the like" are said with reference to the praise. That is, the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, addressing the priests such as the Adhvaryu, says "produce Agni by churning, with mantras"; this

meaning is suggested here. How is Agni free from the nature of death? By offering to Agni fuel and oblations such as ghee, he is always shining without going out: this purport is suggested by the word अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*). Since the churning of fire is one of the rites to be performed at the beginning of the sacrifice, the sacrificer is clearly praying to the Adhvaryu that he should produce Agni by churning; to the Hotṛ that he should recite the mantras prescribed for that churning; to the Udgātṛ that he should sing the Sāma mantras such as the Stoma; to the other priests that they should offer in the fire oblations and the like for the gods; and finally to Agni that he should carry the oblations offered to the gods who are intended.

Mortals, that is, men, praise at the sacrifices with seven strands that Agni, the shining, immortal one, who has not the nature of dying, the best sacrificer in the world of men, that is, among the people connected with men.
- अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*)—free from the nature of death
Men praise in the sacrifices Agni, the shining one, the most worshipful in the human world, who is free from the nature of death.
Mortals worship him, an immortal divinity, at their sacrifices, most adorable among the human race.

मानुषे लोके अध्वरेषु मर्त्याः (*mānuṣe loke adhvareṣu martyāḥ*) praise: in the world of men, that is, on this earth, in the sacrificial rites proceeding on the sacrificial altar, men who are sacrificers praise Agni with various praises: this is the purport.

The many praisers praise that god Agni. What are they like? They are provided with a ladle that pours ghee. For what purpose do they praise him? For the carrying of the oblation, which has the form of cooked rice, cake and the like, to carry it.
- वोढवे (*voḍhave*)—in order to carry (to the gods)
Many praisers, provided with the oblation-vessel that pours streams of ghee, praise that same Agni, who is of divine nature, in order to carry the oblation to the gods.
Numerous (worshippers), pouring out butter from the (sacrificial) ladle, glorify him, the divine Agni, that he may convey their oblation (to the gods).

धृतश्चुता—धृतं क्षरंत्या स्रुचा । (*dhṛtaścutā—dhṛtaṃ kṣaraṃtyā srucā |*) Pouring ghee; that is, when making an offering they fill wooden ladles with ājya (clarified butter) and offer it in the fire. Those ladles are called sruk. Because ghee is poured into the fire from such ladles, they are described by the word धृतश्चुता (*dhṛtaścutā*).

Agni, born, that is, manifested by the churning of the two fire-sticks, slaying the dasyus, the enemies who obstruct the sacrifice, shone, that is, blazed, destroying the darkness by his own light, his own brilliance. Moreover he found गा (*gā*), the waters, and svar, the sun: he made them known. ⟨NOTE:18⟩
notes: ಗಾ ಅಪ ಉದಕಾನಿ: Sāyaṇa glosses only the waters; the Kannada gloss has ಗಾಃ—ಗೋವುಗಳನ್ನೂ

en: - जातः (*jātaḥ*)—as soon as he is born
- दस्यून् (*dasyūn*)—the enemies who cause obstruction to the sacrifice
As soon as he is born, Agni shone, destroying the enemies who cause obstruction to the sacrifice and driving away the darkness by his own radiance. He made the cows, the waters and the sun manifest.
Agni, as soon as born, blazes brightly, destroying the Dasyus, and (dispersing) the darkness by his lustre: he has discovered the cows, the waters, the sun.

In the sacrifice, as soon as Agni is brought forth by the act of churning, the darkness is dispelled by his radiance and everything comes to shine with light. The cows, the waters and the sun as well engaged in their respective functions: this is the main import.

Addressing the people: worship Agni, who is ईळेन्यं (*īḷenyaṃ*), praiseworthy; कविं (*kaviṃ*), far-seeing (क्रांतदर्शिनं (*krāṃtadarśinaṃ*)); and धृतपृष्ठं (*dhṛtapṛṣṭhaṃ*), he whose upper part of the flame. May that Agni desire (कामयतां (*kāmayatāṃ*)) my invocation, that is, my call, and may he hear it.
- धृतपृष्ठं (*dhṛtapṛṣṭhaṃ*)—having a flame whose base is held (fed) by ghee ⟨NOTE:19⟩
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—the praise in the form of an invocation
notes: ಧೃತಮೂಲವಾದ ಜ್ವಾಲೆ in the Kannada gloss; Sāyaṇa has ದೀಪೋಪರಿಭಾಗಂ, the upper part of the flame

en: Worship Agni, who is worthy of praise, far-seeing, and has a flame whose base is held by ghee. May that same Agni know my praise, which takes the form of an invocation, and listen and hear it.
Worship the adorable Agni, the sage, whose summit blazes with butter : may he hear and comprehend my invocation.

धृतसृष्टं—दीप्तोपरिभागं (*dhṛtasṛṣṭaṃ—dīptoparibhāgaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:20⟩ Because ghee (ājya, ghṛta) is offered into the fire, Agni is described by the epithet that speaks of ghee at his summit; that is, by the oblations of ghee Agni blazes up well and shines. The meaning is: worship such a resplendent Agni.
notes: ಧೃತಸೃಷ್ಟಂ here against ಧೃತಪೃಷ್ಠಂ in the verse and bhāṣya; ದೀಪ್ತೋಪರಿಭಾಗಂ against ದೀಪೋಪರಿಭಾಗಂ in the bhāṣya

en: The priests (ऋत्विजो (*ṛtvijo*)) augmented Agni, who is विश्वचर्षणिं (*viśvacarṣaṇiṃ*), the beholder of all, and who is accompanied by the gods, who are स्वाधीभिः (*svādhībhiḥ*), of good meditation, and वचस्युभिः (*vacasyubhiḥ*), desirous of praise; they augmented him with ghee and with स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*), praises, that is, hymns of praise.
- वचस्युभिः (*vacasyubhiḥ*)—and desirous of praise, accompanied by the gods
- विश्वचर्षणिं (*viśvacarṣaṇiṃ*)—having the power to see all
The priests made Agni grow with ghee and with praises: Agni, who is accompanied by gods worthy of excellent meditation and desirous of praise, and who has the power to see all.
They have augmented Agni, the beholder of all, with oblation and with praises, along with the gods, the objects of pious meditations, desirous of praise.

In the sacrifice the priests caused Agni, who is accompanied by gods worthy of meditation and of praise, and who is able to see everything, to blaze and shine by the oblations of ghee offered with mantras. That is, by the oblations of ghee which the priests offer with mantras, Agni blazed and shone: this is the purport.

The Agni who is घृतप्रसत्तो (*ghṛtaprasatto*), gratified by ghee in the form of the oblation; strong; सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*), one whose शेवं (*śevaṃ*), happiness, is good, since शेव (*śeva*) is read among the names of happiness; रायो (*rāyo*) धर्ता (*dhartā*), the supporter, that is, nourisher, of wealth; धरुणो (*dharuṇo*), the holder of the oblations; and वस्वो (*vasvo*), the bestower of dwelling: that Agni is so. To the वेधसे (*vedhase*), creator; कवये (*kavaye*), far-seeing (क्रांतदृशे (*krāṃtadṛśe*)); वेद्याय (*vedyāya*), worthy of praise (the root विदि (*vidi*) here has the same sense as मनि (*mani*), and मनि (*mani*) denotes the act of praising); to the renowned (यशसे (*yaśase*)), the foremost (पूर्वाय (*pūrvāya*), chief): to that Agni I offer (प्र भरे (*pra bhare*), may I present, प्रणयानि (*praṇayāni*)) praise.
- धरुणः (*dharuṇaḥ*)—the one who holds the oblation
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—the giver of dwelling, he is
- पूर्वाय्य (*pūrvāyya*)—and foremost; addressing such an Agni
- प्र भरे (*pra bhare*)—I produce well and offer

Agni is one who is gratified by ghee, powerful, endowed with excellent happiness, the nourisher of wealth, the one who holds the oblation and the giver of dwelling. Addressing that Agni, who is the creator, of far-reaching wisdom, worthy of praise, famous and foremost, I compose excellent praise and offer it.

I offer praise to Agni, the creator, the far-seeing, the adorable, the renowned, the first (of the gods); he who is propitiated by oblations, the strong, the giver of happiness, the possessor of riches, the receiver of oblations, the bestower of dwellings.

The sacrificers (yajamānas) who, in the sacrifice that is the धरुणे (*dharuṇe*), upholder, of दिवो (*divo*), the world of heaven, reach (अभि ननक्षुः (*abhi nanakṣuḥ*), approach) together with the born men, the priests, the unborn gods, the leaders, who are seated (सेदुष आसीनान् (*seduṣa āsīnān*)) there: those sacrificers uphold (धारयंत (*dhārayaṃta*) is धारयंति (*dhārayaṃti*)) with ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), praise, Agni, who is the upholder of the sacrifice and of the nature of truth, in the excellent place, the व्योमन् (*vyoman*), namely the uttaravedi, in the rite (शाके (*śāke*), the occasion of the rite).
- जातैः (*jātaiḥ*)—with the priests who are human beings
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—and of the nature of truth, Agni
- शाके (*śāke*)—that which is the occasion of the rite
- व्योमन् (*vyoman*)—in the place that has the form of the uttaravedi

The sacrificers who bring together, with the human priests, the gods who are seated in the sacrifice that upholds the world of heaven, the leaders, the unborn: those sacrificers have established and made stand, with praise, Agni, the upholder of the sacrifice and of the nature of truth, in the place that has the form of the uttaravedi, which is the occasion of the rite and excellent.

They are detaining by sacrifice the true recipient (of offerings) in the most eminent place of the ceremony, who brings together the leaders (of the rite), the unborn, with the born (or gods and men), as seated at the solemnity which is the stay of heaven.

The sacrificers who offer to that Agni, the foremost (पूर्वाय्य (*pūrvāyya*), chief), abundant food, वयो (*vayo*), in the form of the oblation, which is great (महदधिकं (*mahadadhikaṃ*), exceeding) and hard for the Rākṣasas to obtain: those sacrificers free their own bodies from sin (तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*) is their own bodies; अंहोयुवः (*aṃhoyuvaḥ*) means separating from sin) and extend them (वि तन्वते (*vi tanvate*), they spread them out). May the newly born Agni overcome (तुतुर्यात् (*tuturyāt*), तरतु (*taratu*)) the enemies assembled (संवतः (*saṃvataḥ*), संगतान् (*saṃgatān*)). Moreover, may the enemies who are all around keep away from me and stand apart, as animals keep away from an angry lion.
- दुष्टरं (*duṣṭaraṃ*)—and not to be obtained by the Asuras
- अंहोयुवः (*aṃhoyuvaḥ*)—having made them free of sin
- वि तन्वते (*vi tanvate*)—they cause to grow
- सिंहं न (*siṃhaṃ na*)—as all the animals, afraid of a lion, stand in very distant regions!
- स्थुः (*sthuḥ*)—may they come to stand far away

The sacrificers who offer to the foremost god Agni the oblation that is most abundant and cannot be obtained by the Asuras make their bodies free of sin and cause them to grow. May the newly born Agni drive far away the enemies who have gathered round. As all the animals, afraid of an angry lion, stand in very distant regions, so may all the enemies, afraid at the sight of me, not come near me but stand far away.

They who (present) to the chief (of the gods) the great food (of sacrifice, unattainable {by the Rakshasas), enjoy forms exempt from defect: may that new born Agni scatter assembled (hosts): let them stand from around me, as (deer avoid) an angry lion.

When you, पप्रथानः (*paprathānaḥ*), spreading everywhere, sustain every man like a mother; and when, for support (धायसे (*dhāyase*), धारणाय (*dhāraṇāya*)) and for seeing (चक्षसे (*cakṣase*), दर्शनाय (*darśanāya*)), you are prayed to by all; and when you are being held (दधानो (*dadhāno*), धार्यमाणो (*dhāryamāṇo*)), then you bring to maturity (जरयसि (*jarayasi*)) all food, वयो वयः (*vayo vayaḥ*). Moreover, being विषुरूपो (*viṣurūpo*), of manifold form, you go round all beings by yourself (त्मनात्मना (*tmanātmanā*)).
- धायसे (*dhāyase*)—for the support of the world
- चक्षसे च (*cakṣase ca*)—and also for looking graciously (you are prayed to, when)
- परि जिगासि (*pari jigāsi*)—you pervade everything and make it enter into yourself

O Agni, when, having gained increase everywhere, you bear all people like a mother, and are prayed to for the support of the world and for looking on it with a gracious eye, and when, held by all, you cause all food to ripen, then, possessing forms of many kinds, you pervade everything by your own greatness and make it enter into yourself.

When, everywhere predominating, you cherish all men like a mother, and (are implored by all) to behold and to support them : and when, being detained, you mature every kind of food, then, multiform (Agni), you comprise (all beings) in yourself.

O shining Agni: may the food in the form of the oblation, which is उरुं (*uruṃ*), vast, दोघं (*doghaṃ*), the yielder of desires, and धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*), the supporter, of wealth, guard today the end (अंतं (*aṃtaṃ*), completion, fulfilment) of your strength. As a thief (तायुर् (*tāyur*)) guards an article that he keeps hidden in a cave, so you, for great wealth, that is, for the winning of wealth, showing the good path, gratify the seer Atri.
- देव (*deva*)—O Agni, who are of divine nature
- वाजः (*vājaḥ*)—the food in the form of the oblation
- तायुः न (*tāyuḥ na*)—as a thief carefully guards it

O Agni, who are of divine nature, may the food in the form of the oblation, which is abundant, yields desires and supports wealth, protect your strength entirely. For the winning of great wealth, showing us the good path, protect Atri carefully and gratify him, as a thief who has obtained property hidden in a cave guards it with care.

Divine Agni, may the (sacrificial) food, the vast yielder (of benefits to men), the sustainer of riches, support the utmost of your vigour ; and do you, considering (the means of acquiring) great riches, like a thief keeping concealed the article (he has stolen), be propitious to Atri.

In the sacrifice abundant food, बृहद्वयो (*bṛhadvayo*), in the form of the oblation, is given to the radiant (दीप्तिमते (*dīptimate*)) Agni. Therefore you also offer food (अर्च (*arca*), give) to the shining god Agni, whom men set in front, as a friend, with excellent praises (प्रशस्तिभिः (*praśastibhiḥ*), प्रकृष्टाभिः (*prakṛṣṭābhiḥ*)): they place him first.
Addressing Agni, who is divine and radiant, whom men have established in front of them, praising him with excellent praises as they honour their friends, offer abundant oblation.
Offer abundant (sacrificial) food to the brilliant divine Agni, whom mortals have placed before them by praises as a friend.

The Agni who makes the oblation attached (आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)) among the gods, who is possessed of the splendours (द्युभिर् (*dyubhir*)) of strength in his arms (बाह्वोः (*bāhvoḥ*)), becomes the invoker (होता (*hotā*)) of the gods for the people, that is, the sacrificers. Like Bhaga, that is, like the sun, he bestows especially (व्यृण्वति (*vyṛṇvati*)) desirable wealth (वारं (*vāraṃ*)) upon men.
- स हि अग्निः (*sa hi agniḥ*)—that same god Agni
- होता (*hotā*)—being in the form of the invoking priest
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—he provides (for the gods) in due succession
- भगः न (*bhagaḥ na*)—(and) like the sun
- वि ऋण्वति (*vi ṛṇvati*)—he gives in a special manner

That same god Agni, endowed with the splendours that are the strength of his arms, and being the invoking priest for the sacrificers, provides the oblation in due order and succession to all the gods. And like the sun he supplies men with the wealth they desire.

For that Agni, (endowed) with the lustre of the strength of his arms, is the ministrant priest of mortals, who (presents) the oblation to the gods in succession, and like Bhaga distributes desirable wealth.
भगो न-सूर्य इव (*bhago na-sūrya iva*). Like the sun. As the sun is needed by everyone, so wealth too is a thing needed by everyone. The meaning is that everyone desires it.

May we be in the praise (स्तोमे (*stome*)) and in the friendship of such an Agni: he is मघोनो (*maghono*), the possessor of wealth, and वृद्धशोचिषः (*vṛddhaśociṣaḥ*), one whose splendours, that is, lustres, are great. He is the lord, loud with much sound, in whom all (विश्वे (*viśve*), all the priests) place strength (शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*), बलं (*balaṃ*)) fully, with oblations and with praises.
- सं आदधुः (*saṃ ādadhuḥ*)—have placed in full: of such
- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—and in friendship may we be
notes: ತುವಿಷ್ಟಣಿ here, ತುವಿಷ್ವಣಿ in the Saṃhitā, ತುವಿಸ್ವನಿ in the Pada

en: May we be in the act of praise and in the friendship of this Agni, who is the possessor of wealth and of abundant radiance, who has much sound, who is the lord of all, and in whom all the priests have placed strength.

(May we be assiduous) in the praise, (and cherished) in the friendship, of that very radiant possessor of wealth, on whom, loud-sounding and all-ruling, (his) universal (worshippers) have conferred vigour.
तुविष्टणे बहुशब्दे (*tuviṣṭaṇe bahuśabde*). It is a matter of experience that when a fire is burning it makes a sound such as crackling and so on.

O Agni, then (अध (*adha*) is अथ (*atha*)): for us, the sacrificers, be disposed to giving (मंहना (*maṃhanā*) means दानाय (*dānāya*); the root मंहति (*maṃhati*) is read as a verb of giving) of the excellent strength (सुवीर्यस्य (*suvīryasya*)) that is desired by all. Heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)) have encompassed (परिगृह्णीतः (*parigṛhṇītaḥ*)) that very Agni, glory (श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)) to be heard by all, as they encompass the great sun (यह्वं न (*yahvaṃ na*)).
- यह्वं न (*yahvaṃ na*)—as they surround the great sun

O Agni, after our time of worship, be of gracious mind to give us, the sacrificers, excellent strength and wealth. Heaven and earth both stand surrounding the renowned Agni, as they surround the great sun.
Now verily, Agni, (be disposed) for bestowing excellent strength on these (your worshippers): heaven and earth have invested him with glory like the vast (sun).

O Agni, being praised (गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*), स्तूयमानः (*stūyamānaḥ*)), come quickly to the sacrifice; and having come, bring us desirable wealth (वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*), वरणेयं (*varaṇeyaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:23⟩), that is, provide it. We who are the sacrificers and those who are the praisers (सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*), स्तोतारः (*stotāraḥ*)), both together with oblations (सचा (*sacā*)), offer praise (स्वस्ति (*svasti*), स्तोत्रं (*stotraṃ*); धामहे (*dhāmahe*), we make). And be for our increase and prosperity in the battles (पृत्सु (*pṛtsu*), पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)).
notes: ವರಣೇಯಂ printed; ವರಣೀಯಂ expected

en: - ये वयं (*ye vayaṃ*)—we who are the sacrificers
- ये च (*ye ca*)—and we who are
- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—the praisers, we who worship in both ways
- स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—the praise that goes to meet you

O Agni, praised by us, come to our sacrifice at once. We who are sacrificers and praisers, worshipping you by both kinds of rites, prepared with the oblations, offer the praise that goes to meet you. Be gracious, so that victory and increase may be ours in the battles.

Glorified by us, Agni, come quickly, and bring us desirable wealth : we who (are your worshippers), we (who are your) adorers, offer you welcome together with oblations: be favourable to us; be (our) success in battles.

O god Agni: a mortal, that is, a man, the priest (ऋत्विगित्थेत्थं (*ṛtvigitthetthaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:24⟩), thus calls with sacrifices, that is, with praises, for his gratification (ऊतये (*ūtaye*), तर्पणाय (*tarpaṇāya*)) you, Agni, who are तव्यांसं (*tavyāṃsaṃ*), grown strong by your own splendours. Moreover Pūru, a man and a praiser, in the sacrifice well performed (कृते स्वध्वरे (*kṛte svadhvare*)), praises that Agni for protection (अवसे (*avase*), रक्षणाय (*rakṣaṇāya*)).
notes: ಋತ್ವಿಗಿತ್ಥೇತ್ಥಂ glued as printed

en: - तव्यांसं (*tavyāṃsaṃ*)—you, who have grown by your own splendour
- यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—with praises that are parts of the sacrifice

O Agni, of divine nature, the human priest calls and prays to you, who have grown by your own splendour, for protection, in the prescribed manner, with praises that are parts of the sacrifice. Pūru the praiser, at the time of the performance of an excellent sacrifice, praises Agni for protection.
Divine Agni, a mortal thus with sacrifices (calls upon you) who are endowed with lustre for protection : Puru adores Agni for protection when the sacred rite is solemnized.

पूरुः (*pūruḥ*). In this ṛk the seer has spoken his own name. Although the verbs of the doer are in the third person, their use in the sense of the first person is a special usage current in the Ṛgveda.

Sāyaṇa addresses the praiser: "O Vidharman", that is, one whose dharma is distinguished (viśiṣṭa); this is a vocative for the praiser. The praiser is "svayaśastaraḥ", the most renowned among those of good renown. With a mind of excellent understanding, as his means, he praises with his mouth that well-known Agni (the "hi" marks him as famous). Agni is of this kind: "nāka" is happiness; "aka" is pain; he for whom there is no pain is nāka. He is of wonderful lustre (चित्रतोभिषं (*citratobhiṣaṃ*) is glossed as "of wonderful radiance"), adorable (मंद्रं (*maṃdraṃ*) is glossed as "worthy of praise"), and supreme. ⟨NOTE:25⟩
notes: ಪರಃ ಪರಸ್ತಾಶ್ಚಿತಂ — the gloss of ಪರಃ is damaged in the bhāṣya; not construed

en: - विधर्मान् (*vidharmān*)—O praiser, who have faith in various rites
- नाकं (*nākaṃ*)—him who is free from pain
- परः (*paraḥ*)—who has a power surpassing worldly condition
- तं अस्य हि (*taṃ asya hi*)—that very Agni

O praiser, who with faith perform many rites, you, being of exceeding fame, praise with speech endowed with excellent understanding that very Agni, who is free from pain, of manifold splendour, worthy of praise, and of a power surpassing worldly condition.

Performer of various functions, who are deservedly renowned, you praise by your words that Agni, who is possessed of wonderful splendour ; who is exempt from pain ; who is adorable and supreme in understanding.
नाकं (*nākaṃ*): अकं दुःखं । न विद तेऽकं यस्य सः (*akaṃ duḥkhaṃ | na vida te 'kaṃ yasya saḥ*). "Aka" means pain; the absence of pain is "nāka", that is, happiness. This is the meaning intended.

The Agni who is joined with praise (gir) accompanied by "tuja", that is, a strength able to protect the world, is meant here. Like the shining sun, the whole world is pervaded by the radiance (retas) of whichever Agni it is whose great flames (arcayaḥ, "dīptayaḥ") shine forth. By the radiance of this Agni the sun becomes radiant. The word "u" is a mere filler. ⟨NOTE:26⟩
notes: ದಿವೋ ನ — Sāyaṇa glosses it as "of the shining sun"; the Kannada gloss reads "like the luminous atmosphere (ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷ)"

en: - तुजा (*tujā*)—accompanied by the capacity to protect the world
- दिवो न (*divo na*)—like the luminous atmosphere
- अर्चिषा वै (*arciṣā vai*)—by the radiance alone

The Agni who joins with praise accompanied by the capacity to protect the world, and by whose radiance all the rays, of great form like the luminous atmosphere, shine: by the radiance of that Agni alone the sun too becomes radiant.
He who is endowed with vigour, is (glorified) by praise, and by whose radiance, like that of the sky, the rays of light shine brightly : by his lustre, verily, (the sun is luminous).

In this Ṛk it is described that the sun shines by the radiance of Agni. In many places it is said that Agni shines in heaven (the atmosphere) in the form of the sun, which is one of his three forms. The same idea is indicated here.

The vicetasaḥ are the priests of good understanding. By the kratu, that is, by the rite such as the sacrifice, of this Agni, who is "dasma", pleasing to see, they place (ā dadhati) wealth in the chariot. That Agni, who is to be invoked for the sacrifice, is then, immediately after his birth, praised among all the people (vikṣu, "prajāsu").
- दस्मस्य (*dasmasya*)—of him who has an attractive form
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—as the fruit of the rite of worship
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—who is worthy of the oblation

As the fruit of worshipping this Agni, who has an attractive form, the priests of excellent understanding fill their chariots with wealth. Agni, who is worthy of the oblation, is praised by all the people.
By the worship of him who is pleasing of aspect, the provident (heap) wealth in their cars : Agni, to whom oblations are due, is then grorified by people.

"O Agni, give us quickly (nu) the desirable (vāryam) wealth"; "id" is a filler. For the praisers (sūrayaḥ) obtain wealth from you by their praise (āsā, "āsyena stotreṇa"). Further, O "ūrjo napāt": son of food, or son of strength, that is, "not letting food fall". "Abhiṣṭaye" is for one who desires: the sense to be supplied is "give me food". "Protect us from calamities." "Svastaye": for welfare, for the welfare of wealth such as cattle: "be able" (शग्धि (*śagdhi*)), that is, "I ask you"; the second person is used for the first by interchange. Or it may mean "be able". "And, O Agni, in battles (pṛtsu, "pṛtanāsu") be (edhi, "bhava") for our growth." ⟨NOTE:27⟩
notes: ಮೃಧೇ printed in the bhāṣya for the verse's ವೃಧೇ

en: - उर्जो नपात् (*urjo napāt*)—O Agni, son of strength
- अभिष्टये (*abhiṣṭaye*)—to me, who desire food (give food)
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for the securing of our welfare
notes: ವಿಧಿ printed in the Pratipadārtha; the verse has ಏಧಿ

en: O Agni, grant quickly to us also that same desired wealth which the praisers obtain by their praises. O Agni, son of strength, give food to me, who desire food. Protect me. Be able to secure our welfare. And in battles be a helper for our victory and growth.

Quickly, (Agni, give us) desirable (wealth), such as the devout combining with (pious) praise, (obtain): son of strength, (be favourable) to (my) desires ; protect us (from calamity); be alert for our prosperity ; come for our success in battles.

ऊर्जोनपात् (*ūrjonapāt*): अन्नस्य पातयितः बलस्य पुत्र ना (*annasya pātayitaḥ balasya putra nā*) ⟨NOTE:29⟩. Since the word "ūrjaḥ" has the meanings food and strength, Agni is addressed either as the lord of food, or as the son of strength, that is, one born from the churning done with the use of strength.

शग्गि (*śaggi*): याचे (*yāce*). "I pray." Here the second person singular is used in place of the first person singular. Such usages, and the interchange of case-endings and numbers, are specially employed in the Ṛgveda.
notes: ನಾ printed; the bhāṣya has ವಾ

en: "Puru-priya" is "much loved". "Viśaḥ" is the one who establishes wealth in the sacrificer. He is the "atithi" (guest): one who comes to the houses of the sacrificers on the lunar days (tithi). So Yāska says: अतिथिरभ्यतितो गृहान्भवत्य- (*atithirabhyatito gṛhānbhavatya-*) (the passage breaks off at the end of this page and continues in the next window).

Sāyaṇa completes the quotation from Yāska: भ्येति तिथिषु परकुलानीति वा परगृहाणीति वा (*bhyeti tithiṣu parakulānīti vā paragṛhāṇīti vā*) (Ni. 4-5), that is, one who comes on the lunar days to the families of others or to the houses of others. Such an Agni is praised in the morning ("prātaḥ", "stūyate"). The immortal Agni (one whose nature is not to die) desires ("kāmayate") all the oblations that are placed among mortals, that is, among the sacrificers.
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—who is free from the nature of death
- अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)—worthy of worship like a guest
The immortal Agni, who desires all the oblations that are with the sacrificers, who is wanted by many and is worthy of worship for the sacrificers like a guest, is praised at the time of dawn.
Let Agni, the beloved of many, the guest of man, be present at dawn; he who, immortal, desires the oblations of mortals.

"O Agni, to Dvita", that is, the son of Dvita, who is "mṛktavāhas": one who carries ("vahati", "prāpayati") pure ("mṛkta", "śuddha") oblation to the gods. To him, for your own ("svasya", "ātmīyasya") "dakṣa", that is, strength or wealth, be of a giving mind (मंहना (*maṃhanā*) is explained as "for giving") ⟨NOTE:31⟩.
"O immortal, eternal Agni": because that Mṛktavāhas, always attached to you, holds the "indu", the Soma, and is also your praiser.
notes: ಧನಸ್ಯ ನಾ ಮುಂಹನಾ — ನಾ and ಮುಂಹನಾ as printed; the block continues on the next page with ಮಂಹನಾಯ್ಕೆ

en: - (O Agni) मृक्तवाहसे (*mṛktavāhase*)—who has pure oblation to offer to you
- मंहना (*maṃhanā*)—be one with a mind to give
- अमर्त्य (*amartya*)—O Agni, free from the nature of death
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to offer, with you in view

O Agni, be of a mind to give your own strength to Dvita, who has pure oblation to offer to you. O Agni, free from the nature of death, that Dvita, the Mṛktavāha, at all times, reciting your praise, holds the Soma in order to offer it to you.
Be (willing to make) a grant of your own strength to Dwita, the bearer of the pure oblations ; for he, immortal Agni, your diligent praiser, brings to you continually the Soma juice.

"O Agni, you whose brightness travels far": "vaḥ" is a plural used in honour (of the one addressed). I invoke ("huve", "āhvayāmi") you with praise on behalf of the wealthy ("maghonām"). "O giver of horses": of whichever wealthy men the chariot goes forth ("vīyate", "vigacchatu") unharmed ("ariṣṭaḥ") by enemies in battles.
- (O Agni) दीर्घायुशोचिषं (*dīrghāyuśociṣaṃ*)—who have been shining for many ages

O Agni, you who have been shining for many ages and are renowned, I praise and call you on behalf of the wealthy. O Agni, giver of horses, may the chariot of those same wealthy men travel happily in battles, not harmed by enemies.
I invoke you bright-shining, through a long life, with praise, (for the benefit) of the affluent, that their chariot, giver of horses, may proceed unimpeded.

Among whichever priests there is ("bhavati") varied ("citrā", "nānāvidhā") "dīdhiti", that is, action concerning the sacrifice; who guard in their mouths ("āsan", "āsye") the "ukthāni", that is, the hymns: by those priests, upon the strewn ("stīrṇam") sacred grass ("barhiḥ"), the "śravāṃsi", that is, foods and oblations, are placed ("dadhire", "nidhīyante") in the "svarṇara": "svar" is heaven, and that which leads ("nayati") the sacrificer ("nara") there is the sacrifice, "svarṇara".
- दीधितिः (*dīdhitiḥ*)—actions concerning the sacrifice are performed
- बर्हिः परि (*barhiḥ pari*)—upon the seats of sacred grass
- स्वर्णरे (*svarṇare*)—in the sacrifice that leads the sacrificer to heaven

Those priests who are renowned for performing sacrificial rites of many kinds, who always recite the hymns from their mouths and so guard them, place the oblations, for the sacrificer, upon the widely spread seats of sacred grass in the sacrifices that lead to heaven.

Amongst whom the ceremonial of many kinds is observed ; who perpetuate the sacred hymns by their recital ; by them the sacrificial viands are placed upon the strewn grass (at the sacrifice which) leads (the worshipper) to heaven.

The liberal wealthy men who gave me fifty horses together with praise ("sadhastuti"), that is, immediately after the praise of you: "O immortal Agni", for those wealthy men make ("kṛdhi", "kuru"; the meaning is "give") splendid ("dyumat", "dīptimat"), great ("mahi", "mahat"), abundant ("bṛhat", "parivṛḍham") food ("śravaḥ", "annam"), accompanied by men who attend ("nṛvat", "paricārakamanuṣyayukta").
- सधस्तुति (*sadhastuti*)—immediately after (praising you on their behalf)
- नृवत् (*nṛvat*)—accompanied by sons, grandsons and others

O immortal Agni, for those wealthy men on whose behalf I praised you, and who immediately gave me fifty horses, provide wealth of food that is splendid, great, exceedingly abundant and accompanied by sons, grandsons and others.
Immortal Agni, bestow upon those opulent men, who, upon (my) praise (of you), gave to me fifty horscs, and brilliant, ample, and abundant food, (supporting numerous) dependents.
In this Ṛk the seer says that he has praised Agni on behalf of the wealthy, prays Agni to provide them with wealth such as food, and so praises the generosity of the wealthy.

Of the seer Vanvi (the "vanir"), one after another ("abhi", "uttarottaram") unhappy states ("avasthāḥ", "aśobhanā daśāḥ") arise ("pra jāyante"). Agni, who shares in the oblations, such as he is, is to take full note ("pra ciketa", "prajānīyāt"); the sense is that, having known them, he is to remove them. This is the Agni who sees ("vi caṣṭe", "paśyati") all that exists near ("samīpe") the lap ("upasthe") of the mother, the Earth. ⟨NOTE:33⟩
notes: ವನ್ವೇರ್ಖುಷೇಃ printed at the start of the bhāṣya; ವನಿಃ ಹವಿಷಾಂ ಸಂಭಕ್ತಾ read as Agni

en: - वव्रेः (*vavreḥ*)—to the seer named Vavri (to me) ⟨NOTE:34⟩
- वि चष्टे (*vi caṣṭe*)—looks upon everything, of such a kind
- प्र चिकेत (*pra ciketa*)—let him know fully (the distresses of Vavri) and destroy them
notes: ವಪ್ರಿ printed in the gloss and in the Bhāvārtha for ವವ್ರಿ

en: One after another, circumstances of distress befall the seer named Vavri (me). May Agni, who sitting in the lap of his mother, the Earth, looks upon everything, being the receiver of the oblation, know the distresses of Vavri (mine) and avert them.
Unprosperous circumstances affect Vavri: may the accepter (of oblations) become cognizant (of them), as, reclining on the lap of his mother, he beholds all things.

notes: the Pada-pāṭha of this ṛk ends with ೩; the Saṃhitā has ೨

en: O Agni, the people who, knowing ("vi citayantaḥ") your power, invoke you always ("animiṣam", "sarvadā") for the sacrifice, and having invoked you guard your "nṛṣṇam", your strength, with oblations and with praises: they enter ("ā viviśuḥ", "praviśanti") the firm ("dṛḷhām") city that cannot be taken by enemies. As proof, the Nigama: शतं पूर्भिरायसीभिर्नि पाहि (*śataṃ pūrbhirāyasībhirni pāhi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-3-7) ⟨NOTE:36⟩.
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: - (O Agni) वि चितयंतः (*vi citayaṃtaḥ*)—people who fully know (your power)
- पांति (*pāṃti*)—protect so as to increase it by hymns and the like
- दृळ्हां (*dṛḷhāṃ*)—that cannot be besieged by enemies

O Agni, the people who fully know your power always call you to the sacrifice, performing sacrifice. They protect your strength, increasing it with hymns and the like. They conquer and enter the city that cannot be besieged by enemies.
They who know (your power) invoke you incessantly and nourish (your) strength (by oblations): they dwell in an impregnable city.

"Jantavaḥ" are those who are born ("jāyanta"). "Kṛṣṭayaḥ" are men, the priests. "Madhvā na" is "as with honey", with sweet praise. Or else the particle "na" has the sense of "and", and so "and with honey". "Śvaitreyasya": "śvitra" is the atmosphere; of the Agni who is of lightning, born there, they increase the splendid ("dyumat", "dīptimat") strength. What are the kṛṣṭayaḥ like? "Niṣkagrīvaḥ": those whose necks are adorned with gold, the niṣka; the singular is by interchange. Then "bṛha-". ⟨NOTE:37⟩
notes: the bhāṣya is damaged in ಐಸೈನಯಾ, ಕೃಸ್ಟಯಃ, ಶ್ವತ್ರೇಯಸ್ಯ ಶ್ಶಿತ್ರಮಂತರಿಕ್ಷಂ and ಅದ್ವಲಮಾ; not construed further

en: - निष्कग्रीवः (*niṣkagrīvaḥ*)—those whose necks are adorned with golden ornaments
- मध्वा न (*madhvā na*)—with praises that satisfy like honey
- तैत्रेयस्य (*taitreyasya*)—of Agni who dwells in the atmosphere ⟨NOTE:39⟩
- आ वर्धंत (*ā vardhaṃta*)—they cause to increase
notes: ಕೃಷ್ಣಯಃ printed; the verse has ಕೃಷ್ಟಯಃ
ತೈತ್ರೇಯಸ್ಯ printed; the verse has ಶ್ವೈತ್ರೇಯಸ್ಯ

en: The people, priests and others, who have necks adorned with golden ornaments, who have abundant praise, who desire food, and who have been born, cause to increase, with praises that satisfy like honey, the splendid strength of Agni who dwells in the atmosphere.
Living men, with collars of gold, earnest in praise, desirous of food, augment by this laudation the vigour of you abiding in the white firmament.

May Agni, the helper ("sacā") of the two kinsfolk ("jāmyoḥ"), heaven and earth, hear our dear praise, which is desirable ("kāmyam", "kamanīyam"), faultless ("ajāmi", "doṣarahitam"), like milk that has been drawn ("dugdham na payaḥ"). Of what kind is this Agni? Like the "gharma", the Pravargya, he is "vājajaṭharaḥ": he in whose belly is "vāja", food; as the gharma is filled with the offering, with ghee and milk, so he is filled with oblation. "Adabdhaḥ" is one not hurt by enemies himself; "śaśvataḥ" is eternal; "dabhaḥ" is the one who harms enemies.
- घर्मो न (*gharmo na*)—as the Pravargya is filled with oblations of many kinds
- वाजजठरः (*vājajaṭharaḥ*)—he who has a belly filled with food
- अदब्धः (*adabdhaḥ*)—he who is not exposed to the harm of enemies
- दभः (*dabhaḥ*)—he who harms enemies, such Agni
- जाम्योः सचा (*jāmyoḥ sacā*)—together with his kinsfolk, heaven and earth
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—this praise of ours; may he hear it

May Agni, who like the Pravargya filled with oblations of many kinds has a belly filled with food, who is not exposed to the harm of enemies and who for ever harms enemies, together with his kinsfolk, heaven and earth, hear this faultless praise of ours, beneficial like milk.

May (Agni) with his two relatives, (heaven and earth), hear this faultless (praise), acceptable as milk : he who like the mixed oblation, is filled with food, and, unsubdued, is ever the subduer of his foes.

"O rays-possessing Agni, playing ("krīḍan") in the forests, with the ashes ("bhasmanā", the burnt remains of your own work) and with Vāyu, the impelling Maruts, well ("saṃ") known ("vevidānaḥ", "samyag jñāyamānaḥ"), be ("ā bhuvaḥ") turned towards us." "Vakṣaṇesthāḥ" are those that stand in the fire ("vahni"); the "vakṣyaḥ" are the flames that carry the oblation. Those well-sharpened ("susaṃśitāḥ", "sutīkṣṇāḥ") flames, "dhṛṣajaḥ", that is, assailants of enemies, are not to be ("na tigmāḥ", "na tīkṣṇāḥ") sharp towards this sacrificer, me ("san" is "santu").
- वायुना (*vāyunā*)—with the help of the wind
- सं वेविदानः (*saṃ vevidānaḥ*)—you who are visible to all
- आ भुवः (*ā bhuvaḥ*)—be turned towards us
- न तिग्माः सन् (*na tigmāḥ san*)—let them not be sharply burning (let them not harm)
notes: ಭಸ್ಮತಾ printed; the verse has ಭಸ್ಮನಾ

en: O Agni, who have rays, you who play in the forest with your ashes and are visible to all with the help of the wind, be turned towards us. May those flames of yours, which stand in the fire, are sharp, are enemy-seeing ⟨NOTE:41⟩ and carry the oblation, not burn sharply in regard to this sacrificer (let them not harm).
notes: ಶತ್ರುದರ್ಶಕ printed in the Bhāvārtha; the Pratipadārtha has ಶತ್ರುಧರ್ಷಕ

en: Radiant (Agni), you are made manifest by the wind, and are supporting amidst the ashes (of the forest); be present with us : and may the fierce fiery flames, destructive of foes, be gentle to this your worshipper.

"O Agni, O Vājasātama", O one who gives food in the highest degree: whatever wealth ("rayim") in the form of oblation, given by us, you approve ("manyase", "budhyase"); ("cit" is a mere filler) that wealth of ours, in the form of oblation, which is worthy to be heard ("śravāyyam", "śravaṇīyam", "śasyam") and is joined ("yujam", "yuktam") with praises ("gīrbhiḥ"), convey ("panaya", "prāpaya") to the gods ("devatrā").
- यं रयिं (*yaṃ rayiṃ*)—which wealth, in the form of our oblation
- मन्यसे (*manyase*)—you approve, of such a kind
O Agni, who give food in abundance, convey to the gods that same oblation of ours, praiseworthy and joined with praises, which is the wealth in the form of oblation that you approve.
That (sacrificial) wealth, Agni, bounteous giver of food, of which you approve, and which deserves to be commended by our praises, convey to the gods

O Agni, those men who are prosperous with wealth in the form of cattle and the like, yet do not offer you oblations, are deprived of strength or food, and so become destitute of strength and food. Further, the Asura whose observance (vrata, rite) is other than the Vedic, set apart from it, incurs your enmity and your violence, that is, severe punishment; they bring these upon themselves.
- वृद्धाः (*vṛddhāḥ*)—even though they have attained increase of wealth
- अन्यव्रतस्य (*anyavratasya*)—those who, leaving the Vedic rite, are performers of non-Vedic rites

O Agni, those men who do not offer you oblations, even though they have attained increase of wealth, become destitute of great strength. And men who have left the Vedic rite and fallen from their duty receive your enmity and violence from you.
May those prosperous men who do not offer oblations to you become destitute of great strength, and may (the followers) of other (than Vaidik) observances incur (your) enmity and punishment.

O Agni, we who are called Prayasvats, that is, possessors of food, choose you as hotṛ, the summoner of the gods, you who are the accomplisher, the one who brings about, of strength. Moreover, you who are foremost, the chief, at sacrifices, we call upon with speech in the form of praise; that is, we praise you.
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—as the one who calls the gods to the sacrifice (as hotṛ)
O Agni, we who are called Prayasvats choose you, the accomplisher of strength, as hotṛ. We pray to you, the chief at the sacrifice, and call upon you with words of praise.
We, Prayasvats, have recourse to you, the invoker (of the gods), the means of strength : we glorify you first at sacrifices with praise.

O Agni, possessor of strength, day after day do so (ittha), act in such a way that we may be in your protection. O doer of good deeds, act so that we may be (devoted) to wealth and to the sacrifice. Moreover, may we rejoice together with cattle, and rejoice together with sons, who are heroes (vīra); act so.
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever manner it should be
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Agni, performer of excellent works

O Agni, endowed with strength, grant that we may be in your protection every day. O Agni, performer of excellent works, grant that we may be intent on sacrificial rites for the gain of wealth, and as the result of it may rejoice together with cattle and with heroic sons.

Possessor of strength, day by day so (provide), that we may enjoy your protection; doer of good deeds, may we (be deserving) of wealth through sacrifice, and may we be happy with cattle, happy with male descendants.

O Agni, we meditate upon you as Manu did (manuṣvat), like Manu. Like Manu we kindle you; that is, we cause you to blaze with kindling-sticks. O Agni, Aṅgiras, of the nature of coals (aṅgāra), worship the gods for the sacrificer who desires the gods, as for Manu, the descendant of Manu.
- अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*)—O Aṅgiras, of the nature of coals
- देवयते (*devayate*)—on behalf of the sacrificer who desires the gods as helpers

O Agni, as Manu meditated upon you, so do we also meditate upon you. As Manu caused you to blaze, so do we also. O Agni, of the nature of coals, for the sacrificer who desires to win the favour of the gods, do you also, like Manu, perform the sacrifice addressing the gods.
Like Manu, we mediate, Agni, upon you ; like Manu, we kindled you : worship the gods on behalf of the (worshipper), devout as Manu.

O Agni, you who are well pleased with praises in the human world (among the human race) are kindled, that is, you shine. The ladles, filled with oblations, come to you, reach you, constantly (ānuṣak, without break). O well-born one, O Agni, to whom clarified butter is poured, possessed of food mixed with ghee.
- सुप्रीतः (*suprītaḥ*)—when you are well satisfied with praises and the like
- मानुषे जने (*mānuṣe jane*)—in the assembly of men
- सर्पिरासुते (*sarpirāsute*)—you who have food in the form of ghee, O Agni

O Agni, when you are satisfied with praises and the like, you blaze forth in the assembly of men. O Agni, of excellent birth and having food in the form of ghee, the ladles filled with oblations continually approach you.
When you are pleased, Agni, you shine upon the human race; well-born, feeder upon clarified butter, the ladles are constantly uplifted to you.

All the gods, being pleased together (sajoṣasaḥ), have made you their messenger (dūta). For this reason, O Kavi, far-seeing one, the sacrificers, serving you who are shining (deva), at the sacrifices praise you; that is, they beseech you in order to summon the gods.

O wise Agni, all the gods, who have equal affection for you, have chosen you as their messenger. Therefore the sacrificers, worshipping at the sacrifices, praise you, who are divine in nature and shining.
All the consenting divinities have made you their messenger ; therefore the pious worship you who are divine, wise Agni, at sacrifices.

The mortal, the man, is fit to praise the shining Agni, the foremost, for the sake of the worship of the gods (devayajyā), that is, in order to sacrifice to the gods. O bright (śukra) Agni, possessed of splendour, kindled, grown strong with oblations, blaze. Of Sasa, the seer, who is truthful (ṛta), take your seat in the place of origin (yoni), the cause of origin, the means of reaching heaven, the place of sacrifice; sit there in the form of a deity. ⟨NOTE:43⟩ The repetition (of "āsadaḥ") is to show great respect.
notes: ಸಸಸ್ಯ ಋಷೇರ್ಮನು ಯೋನಿಂ: ಮನು after ಋಷೇಃ is unclear in the bhāṣya

en: - अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—and of the nature of Agni
- देवयज्यया (*devayajyayā*)—in order to perform the sacrifice addressed to the gods
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—when you are kindled with oblations and the like

- Or else: ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice; योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—in the place of origin; आसदः (*āsadaḥ*)—be seated; ससस्य (*sasasya*)—of the seer named Sasa; योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—in the place of sacrifice; आसदः (*āsadaḥ*)—be seated.

O Agni, a man praises you, who are shining and divine in nature, in order to perform the sacrifice addressed to the gods. O Agni, endowed with radiance, kindled with oblations and the like, shine. Be seated in the place of sacrifice, true in nature, of the seer named Sasa, the follower of truth.
Man praises you, divine Agni, to convey his offerings to the Gods; bright Agni, blaze when kindled : take your seat in the chamber (of sacrifice): in the chamber of the sincere Sasa.

O Viśvasāman: this is an address to the seer. Like Atri, sing forth (prārca, pragāya) to Agni, whose radiance purifies (pāvakaśociṣe). That Agni who is to be praised (īḍya) at the sacrifices by all sacrificers, the hotṛ, the summoner of the gods, is the most praiseworthy among the people (viś).
- होता (*hotā*)—is of the nature of the hotṛ
- प्र अर्च (*pra arca*)—recite an excellent praise

O seer named Viśvasāman, as the seer Atri recited, recite an excellent praise addressed to Agni, who is most worthy of worship at the sacrifices, is of the nature of the hotṛ, is the most praiseworthy among all people, and has a purifying radiance.
Sing, Vishwasaman, like Atri, (a hymn) to the dispencer of purifying light : (to him) who is to be praised at sacrifices, the invoker of the gods, the most adorable by man.

O sacrificers, establish (ni dadhāta) Agni Jātavedas, the one endowed with knowledge or possessor of wealth that has arisen, the shining one, the priest (ṛtvij), the sacrificer at the proper time. Moreover, may the sacrifice, that is, the oblation given by us as the means of sacrifice, which is the dearest (devavyacastama) to the gods, go forth to that Agni today, on this day, continuously (ānuṣak).
- जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—(O sacrificers) endowed with the power of knowing everything that has arisen
- ऋत्विजं (*ṛtvijaṃ*)—in the form of the chief priest of the sacrifice
- नि दधात (*ni dadhāta*)—establish (on the sacrificial ground)
- देवव्यचस्तमः (*devavyacastamaḥ*)—most dear to all the gods
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—the oblation offered in the sacrifice

O sacrificers, establish on the sacrificial ground Agni, who has the power of knowing everything that has arisen, who is shining and is in the form of the chief priest of the sacrifice. May the oblation offered in the sacrifice, most dear to all the gods, continuously join Agni in this sacrifice.
Cherish the divine Agni, by whom all that exists is known, the priest (of the rite): may the sacrifice most suitable for the gods duly this day proceed to them.

O Agni, you who are cikitvin-manas, one whose mind is knowing. We mortals, men, approaching you, the god, for protection, praise you for the satisfaction of your favour (avas), you who are to be shared in (varenya), worthy of being resorted to.
- चिकित्सत्मनसं (*cikitsatmanasaṃ*)—possessed of mental power that knows everything

O Agni, we men, who approach you for protection, you who are possessed of a mental power that knows everything and are divine in nature, praise you for the satisfaction of you who are worthy of worship and honoured.
Men have recourse to you divine Agni, who are of intelligent mind, for security : we praise you who are most excellent, seeking your protection.

O Agni, O Sahasya, son of strength (sahas), know this our service, this speech, this praise. O Suśipra, the one whose jaws or nostrils (śipra) are handsome; the word is an address to him. O Suśipra, of fine jaws, O Dampati, lord of the house, the sons of Atri make you grow with their stomas, praises; the sons of Atri adorn you with their words.
- सहस्य (*sahasya*)—O you, the son of strength
- इदं वचः (*idaṃ vacaḥ*)—this praise, which is worthy of worship
- दंपते (*daṃpate*)—and who are the lord of the house
- वर्धंति (*vardhaṃti*)—make you grow strong and increase

O Agni, son of strength, know the nature of this praise of ours, which belongs to this sacrifice and is worthy of worship. The sons of Atri make you, who have excellent cheeks and are the lord of the house, grow strong with hymns. The same sons of Atri adorn you with words of praise. (They praise you.)

Agni, son of strength recognize the words of this our (laudation): handsome-chinned, lord of the dwelling, the sons of Atri exalt you, such (as you are), by their praises : they embellish you by their hymns.

O Agni, bring (ā bhara) to me, Dyumna, a son (rayi) who overcomes his foes with surpassing strength, as wealth. Here the genitive stands in the sense of the dative. He now explains this: the son who, endowed with praise (āsā, by the mouth), subdues in battles all the men, the enemies, who come against him.
- आसा (*āsā*)—having a mouth (filled with your praise)
- अभि (*abhi*)—who has come to meet him
O Agni, provide to me, named Dyumna, such a son of excellent strength as, with a mouth that praises you alone in battles, has the power to slay all the enemies who face him.
Bestow, Agni, upon Dyumna a son, overcoming foes by his prowess ; one who may with glory subdue all men in battle.
O Agni, O mighty one, bring (ā bhara) a son who overcomes armies (pṛtanā), the enemy hosts. For you are true, in truth wonderful, great, the giver of food (vāja) accompanied by cattle.
- पृतनासहं (*pṛtanāsahaṃ*)—having the strength to overcome the enemy army
O Agni, endowed with strength, provide me with a son who has the strength to overcome the enemy army. You are true in nature, great in form, and the giver of food accompanied by cattle.
Mighty Agni, grant us a son able to encounter hosts ; for you are true and wonderful, and the giver of food with cattle.
O Agni, all the people, the priests (ṛtvij), being pleased together (sajoṣasaḥ), with the sacred grass (barhis) cut, at the sacrificial houses (sadman), you, the hotṛ, the summoner of the gods…
…you, who are dear (priya), pleasing to all, they ask for (vyanti) much (puru) choice wealth.
- व्यक्तबर्हिषः (*vyaktabarhiṣaḥ*)—who have prepared the cut darbha grass as seats
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—of the nature of the hotṛ

O Agni, all the priests, who have equal devotion and affection, and who have cut the darbha grass and arranged excellent seats, ask you, who are of the nature of the hotṛ and dear to all, in the sacrificial houses for abundant and desired wealth.
All men concurring in satisfaction, bearing the clipt sacred grass, solicit you, as the kind invoker of the gods, to the chambers (of sacrifice) for infinite wealth.

O Agni, may that well-known sage Viśvacarṣaṇi hold (dadhe) strength (sahas) that destroys enemies. ⟨NOTE:45⟩ O bright (śukra) Agni, possessed of splendour, shine in our houses (kṣaya) in such a way that they are rich in wealth (revat). O Pāvaka, Agni, purifier of sins, shine with brilliance and with glory (dyumat).
notes: ವಿಶ್ವಚರ್ಷಣಿರ್ಯಷಿಃ and ಹಿ ಸ್ಮೃತಿ ಪೂರಣೌ in the bhāṣya are damaged; read here as ಋಷಿಃ and the particles hi, sma as expletives

en: - एषु क्षयेषु (*eṣu kṣayeṣu*)—in these sacrificial houses
- रेवत् (*revat*)—so that there is abundance of wealth

O Agni, may the seer well known by the name Viśvacarṣaṇi obtain strength that destroys enemies. You, endowed with radiance, shine in these our sacrificial houses so that wealth may abound. O Agni, the purifier, spread your rays everywhere and blaze so as to be most brilliant.
May the (sage) on whom all men rely possess foe-subduing strength : radiant Agni, so shine in our habitations that they may abound in riches : shine, purifying Agni, dispensing light.

O Agni, who are to be chosen (*varūthya*), that is, to be resorted to; or else, enclosed by encircling fences (*varūthaiḥ*), be nearest to us. Be also our protector and the giver of welfare. Agni is the dweller (*vasu*), the foremost of all; being rich in food (*vasuśravas*), turn towards us and reach us; give us most brilliant wealth, wealth in the form of cattle and the like; bestow it on us.
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—the leader of all, as it were
- वसुश्रवाः (*vasuśravāḥ*)—you who are the distributor of food

O worshipful Agni, be exceedingly near to us, our protector and the bringer of welfare. You, who are the giver of dwellings, the leader of all, as it were, and the distributor of food, be turned towards us and pervade us. Give us most radiant wealth.
Agni, you are to be adored, be ever nigh to us, our protector and benefactor : you, who are the giver of dwellings and dispenser of food, be present with us : bestow upon us most brilliant wealth.

O Agni, that you (*sa*) understand us (*bodhi*, "know us"); hear (*śrudhi*) our invocation. Protect (*uruṣya*) us from all men who wish us harm (*aghāyataḥ*, "who desire evil"). O most radiant (*śociṣṭha*), blazing with your own splendours (*dīdivaḥ*), Agni: to you, for the sake of happiness (*sumna*; "*sumna*" is a name of happiness) and for the sake of our friends (*sakhibhyaḥ*), that is, our sons who share one name with us, we now (*nūnam*) make our petition (*īmahe*, "we beg").
- दीदिवः (*dīdivaḥ*)—O Agni, who shine with those radiances
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—for the sake of our dear sons
notes: ಸಮಸ್ತಾತ್ in the gloss; the Saṃhitā block and the bhāṣya have ಸಮಸ್ಮಾತ್

en: O Agni, renowned as you are, understand our devotion. Hear our invocation made with praise. Protect us from all enemies who wish us harm. O Agni, of exceeding radiance, shining with those radiances, we now praise you for happiness and for the sake of our dear sons.
Understand us, Agni; hear our invocation; defend us from all malevolent (people) : most bright and resplendent Agni, we earnestly solicit you for the happiness (of ourselves) and our friends.

O Vasūyus (you who desire wealth), sing forth (*gāsi*, "praise") to the divine Agni for protection. Agni, the dweller (*vasu*), who makes himself dwell in the houses of the sacrificers for the agnihotra, may he (*sa*) grant (*rāsat*) us our desires. He is the son (*putra*) of the seers (*ṛṣūṇām*): because he is produced by the seers by churning, he is called "son" figuratively. Truthful (*ṛtāvā*), that is, possessed of truth, or possessed of water, that Agni may carry us across (*parṣati*) our enemies (*dviṣaḥ*), that is, ferry us over them.
- वसुः (*vasuḥ*)—dwelling in the house of the sacrifice
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—in the form of a son (born by churning and the like)
notes: the gloss line "ಋತಾನಾಸತ್ಯವಂತನೂ ಆದ ಅಗ್ನಿಯು" has the word ಋತಾ run together with ನಾ; read as "truthful"; the Pada block has ಋತ್ಯವಾ for ಋತಾವಾ

en: O seers named Vasūyu, sing the praise of Agni, divine in nature, in a commendable manner, for protection. May that Agni, who dwells in the house of the sacrifice, grant us our desires. May Agni, who, being produced by churning and the like, is as a son to the seers, and who is truthful, destroy our enemies.
Celebrate the divine Agni for his protection : may he who presides over dwellings grant (our desires) : may the son of the Rishis, the observers of truth, save us from those who hate us.

The ancient (*pūrve cit*) great seers kindled Agni, the invoker (*hotāra*) of the gods, whose tongue gives delight (*mandrajihva*): his tongue delights the gods by the offering of oblations; or else, "of delighting tongue". So Yāska says: मंद्रजिह्वं मंदनजिह्वं मोदनजिह्वमिति वा (*maṃdrajihvaṃ maṃdanajihvaṃ modanajihvamiti vā*), Ni. 6-23. He is joined with fair radiances (*sudītibhiḥ*) and has light as his wealth (*vibhāvasu*). The gods too (*devāsaś cit*) kindled that Agni (*īdhire*, "kindled"); that Agni is indeed true (*satya*): he is true to his promise. The word *it* is a filler.
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the invoker for the whole sacrifice
- मंद्रजिह्वं (*maṃdrajihvaṃ*)—he whose flame, in the form of a tongue, gives delight
- सुदीतिभिः (*sudītibhiḥ*)—he who is joined with commendable brilliance
- सत्य (*satya*)—is of the nature of truth

Agni is the invoker for the whole sacrifice; he has a delighting flame in the form of a tongue; he is joined with commendable brilliance; he has radiance as his wealth. The ancient seers and the gods too kindled him; that Agni is truly of the nature of truth.
That Agni is true whom the ancients, whom the gods have kindled, as the bright-tongued invoker of the gods, radiant with holy splendours.

O Agni, praised with fair praises (*suvṛktibhiḥ*, "with hymns") and worthy of being chosen (*vareṇya*): you, with our best (*variṣṭhayā*, "most choice") and most excellent, praiseworthy (*śreṣṭhayā*) service (*dhītī*, our act of attendance), and with our *sumati*, which here means a śastra, being pleased with the śastra, give (*dīdihi*) us riches (*rāyaḥ*, "wealth").
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—he who is praised with excellent praises
- वरिष्ठया (*variṣṭhayā*)—with what is the very best
- सुमत्या च (*sumatyā ca*)—and with praises in the form of śastras (being gratified)

O Agni, praised with excellent praises and greatly honoured, renowned as you are, be gratified with our very best and praiseworthy acts worthy of worship and with our praises in the form of śastras, and give us riches.
Agni, to be propitiated by praises, (gratified) by our choice and most excellent adoration and hymns, bestow upon us riches.
