The Agni who shines (*rājati*) among the gods, that is, appears in the form of a deity in their midst; the Agni who has entered (*āviśan*) among mortals (*marteṣu*), that is, men, in the form of the Āhavanīya and the other fires; the Agni who is the bearer of our oblations (*havyavāhana*), that is, the carrier of the oblations to the deities in our sacrifices: O sacrificers, serve (*saparyata*, "attend upon") that Agni with praises (*dhībhiḥ*).
- राजति (*rājati*)—shines in the form of a deity
- आविशन् (*āviśan*)—has entered in the form of the Āhavanīya and the others
- हव्यवाहनः (*havyavāhanaḥ*)—is the bearer of the oblation (to the gods)

The worshipful Agni shines among the gods in the form of a deity. Agni has entered among men in the form of the Āhavanīya and the other fires. That same Agni is for us the bearer of the oblation to the gods. O sacrificers, worship such a worshipful Agni with praises.
Agni shines amongst the gods: Agni is present amongst mortals : Agni is the bearer of our oblations : glorify Agni with praises.

In the Putrakāmeṣṭi (the offering for the wish for a son), the two Ṛks beginning "Agnis tu viśravastamam" are the yājyā and the anuvākyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt. So it is laid down in the sūtra: अग्निस्तुविश्रवस्तममिति द्वे संयाज्ये (*agnistuviśravastamamiti dve saṃyājye*), Ā. 2-10. Agni, who is of exceeding great fame in food (*viśravastama*, "exceedingly abounding in food"), of many praises (*tuvibrahmāṇa*, "of much hymning"), most excellent (*uttama*), unharmed by enemies (*atūrta*), and *śrāvayatpati*: he makes the lords (*pati*) famous (*śrāvayati*), that is, by his own deeds he makes the fathers known, hence *śrāvayatpati*; ⟨NOTE:48⟩ may Agni give such a son to the sacrificer (*dāśuṣe*) who has given oblations.
notes: ಪತೀನ್ ಪಾಲಯಿತ್ಥನ್ಪಿತ್ಯನಿತಿ ಸ್ವಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಪಿತ್ಯಣಾಂ: the machine-read words are damaged; the sense is taken from the Kannada gloss

en: - दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- तुविक्रवस्तमं (*tuvikravastamaṃ*)—endowed with very abundant wealth of food ⟨NOTE:49⟩
- तुविब्रह्माणं (*tuvibrahmāṇaṃ*)—who composes praise in great measure
- श्रवयत्पतिं (*śravayatpatiṃ*)—who by his excellent deeds brings fame to all his fathers, grandfathers and the rest
notes: ತುವಿಕ್ರವಸ್ತಮಂ printed; the Saṃhitā and bhāṣya have ವಿಶ್ರವಸ್ತಮಂ

en: May Agni favour the sacrificer who offers the oblation with a son who is endowed with very abundant wealth of food, who in great measure composes praises of the deities, who is possessed of excellent qualities, who is not harmed by enemies, and who by his excellent deeds brings fame to all his fathers, grandfathers and the rest.
May Agni bestow upon the donor (of the oblation) a son, abounding in food, abounding in devotion, excellent, unharmed, conferring honour upon his progenitors.

In the sacrifice called Putrakāmeṣṭi, this Ṛk "Agnis tu viśravastamam" and the Ṛk after it are to be recited as the yājyā and anuvākyā mantras in the Sviṣṭakṛt homa, as is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: अग्निस्तु विश्रवस्तममिति द्वे संयाज्ये (*agnistu viśravastamamiti dve saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-10).

The son who in battle (*yudhā*), with his men (*nṛbhiḥ*, his retinue), overcomes (*sasāha*) his enemies, the protector of the good (*satpati*): Agni gives such a son; may he give him to us. Further, Agni (may give) a horse that is *raghuṣyada*: *raghu* is light, *syada* is speed, he whose speed is light; a conqueror (*jetāra*) of enemies, unconquered (*aparājita*) by enemies; *atya* is the horse (*atta*), because it goes (*atati*) constantly. May he give that.
- ससाह (*sasāha*)—defeats the enemies, such a one
- सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*)—and the protector of the good, such a son
- ददाति (*dadāti*)—may he favour us with and give

May Agni favour us with a son who defeats enemies in battles together with his followers and who is the protector of the good. May that same Agni give a horse that is swift-going, conquering enemies, and unconquered by enemies.
May Agni bestow a son, the protector of the good, who, with his followers, may be victorious in battle : may he bestow a swift-footed steed, conquering, unconquered.

At the Aśvamedha, in the offering to Pūṣan (⟨NOTE:50⟩), the Ṛk "Yad vāhiṣṭham" is the yājyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt. So it is laid down in the sūtra: यद्वाहिष्ठं तदग्नय इति संयाज्ये (*yadvāhiṣṭhaṃ tadagnaya iti saṃyājye*), Ā. 10-6. That hymn (*stotra*) which is best at carrying (*vāhiṣṭha*, "most conveying") is made for Agni. Therefore, O Agni, whose wealth is light (*vibhāvaso*; ⟨NOTE:51⟩), give us abundant (*bṛhat*) food or wealth (*arca*, "give"). If it is asked how he can be the giver of food and wealth, he says: because from you
... from you great (*mahiṣī*) wealth (*rayi*) rises up (*udīrate*), and foods (*vājāḥ*) also rise up from you. The word *iva* is a filler.
notes: ಪೌಷ್ಣಾ ಮಿಷ್ಟ printed
ವಿಧಾವಸೋ printed in the bhāṣya

en: - वाहिष्ठं (*vāhiṣṭhaṃ*)—carries our devotion in the highest degree
- विभावसो (*vibhāvaso*)—O Agni, whose wealth is radiance

That hymn which carries our devotion in the highest degree is offered to Agni. O Agni, whose wealth is radiance, give us abundant wealth, for abundant wealth and foods arise from you alone and spread forth.
That (praise) which best conveys (our veneration, is due) to Agni : affluent in splendour, grant us, (Agn'), great (wealth), for from you vast riches and ample food proceed.

In the Pauṣṭa offering (⟨NOTE:52⟩) of the Aśvamedha sacrifice, this Ṛk "Yad vāhiṣṭham" is to be recited as the yājyā mantra of the smitakṛt homa ⟨NOTE:53⟩, as is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: यद्वाहिष्ठं तदग्नय इति संयाज्ये (*yadvāhiṣṭhaṃ tadagnaya iti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 10-6).
notes: ಪೌಷ್ಟೇಷ್ಟಿ printed; the bhāṣya has ಪೌಷ್ಣಾ ಮಿಷ್ಟ
ಸ್ಮಿತಕೃದ್ಧೋಮ printed; the bhāṣya has ಸ್ವಿಷ್ಟಕೃತ್

en: O Agni, your rays (*arcayaḥ*) are radiant (*dyumantaḥ*), full of light. You, who are great (*bṛhat*), are praised (*ucyate*) like the pressing stone (*grāveva*, the stone for pressing). And of you, who shine from the sky (*divaḥ*), by your own power (*tmanā*) your sound (*snānaḥ*) rises (*arta*, "goes up") like thunder (*tanyatuḥ*), the rumbling of a cloud.
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—you, who are of great nature
- ग्रावेव (*grāveva*)—like the stone that presses Soma
- तन्यतुः यथा (*tanyatuḥ yathā*)—like the rumbling of a cloud

O Agni, your rays are full of radiance. You, who are of great nature, are praised like the stone that presses Soma. And your sound, shining by your own greatness, arises and spreads like the rumbling of a cloud.
Brilliant, Agni, are your rays : mighty are you termed, like the stone (that bruises the Soma), and your voice spontaneously spreads through the sky like thunder.

We, the Vasūyus (*vasūyavaḥ*, those who desire wealth), have thus praised (*vavandima*, "we praise") in the manner stated Agni, who is *sahasāna*, that is, who acts like our own strength. May that Agni, the doer of fair works (*sukratu*), carry us over (*parṣat*, "take us across") all (*viśvāḥ*) our enemies (*dviṣaḥ*). How? As with a boat (*nāvā*), a means, one crosses a river.
- वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*)—we, who desire wealth (the seers named Vasūyu)
- सहसानं (*sahasānaṃ*)—who accomplishes works endowed with strength
- नाना इव (*nānā iva*)—as one easily crosses a river with a boat ⟨NOTE:54⟩
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—may he carry across
notes: ತ್ರಿವೃಷ್ಟಸ್ಯ in the bhāṣya, but ತ್ರಿವೃಷ್ಣ in the Kannada Anuvāda

en: We, who are named Vasūyu and desire wealth, praise Agni, who can accomplish works endowed with strength. As one easily crosses a river with a boat, may Agni, the doer of excellent works, carry us across all enemies and protect us.
Thus we, Vasuyus, glorify the vigorous Agni : may he, the performer of great deeds, enable us to pass over our enemies as (we cross a river) with a boat.

O purifier (*pāvaka*), O shining (*deva*) Agni, with your own radiance (*rociṣā*) and with your tongue (*jihvayā*) that delights the gods (*mandrayā*), bring (*vakṣi*) the gods for the sacrifice, and sacrifice (*yakṣi*) also. ⟨NOTE:56⟩
notes: ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ಸುತೋ printed in the bhāṣya; ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ ಸ್ತುತಃ expected

en: - जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—and in the form of tongues
- आ वक्षि (*ā vakṣi*)—bring to the sacrifice
- यक्षि च (*yakṣi ca*)—and sacrifice to them
O Agni, purifier and of divine nature, with flames that are radiant, delighting and in the form of tongues, bring the gods to the sacrifice. Sacrifice to them.
Divine purifier, Agni, with your radiant and pleasing tongue, bring hither and worship the gods.

O *dhṛtasnu*, impeller of ghee (*dhṛta*); or else, born of ghee. O *citrabhānu*: *citrā* means of many kinds, *bhānu* means rays; he who has these is Citrabhānu; this is the address to him. You who see everything (*svardṛśam*), we beg (*īmahe*, "we ask") you; therefore bring the gods for the eating of the oblations (*vītaye*).
- धृतस्नो (*dhṛtasno*)—he who is kindled by ghee
- चित्रभानो (*citrabhāno*)—O Agni, who has rays of many kinds
notes: ತ್ವಾಶಿರಃ printed in the bhāṣya; Saṃhitā has ತ್ರ್ಯಾಶಿರಃ

en: O Agni, kindled by ghee and having rays of many kinds, we pray to you, who can see everything and are renowned. Bring the gods to eat the oblation.
Feeder upon butter, bright and variegated radiance we solicit you, the beholder of heaven, to bring the Gods hither to (partake of) the (sacrificial) food

O seer (*kave*), O Agni of far-reaching sight, you whose sacrifice is desired (*vītihotra*), radiant (*dyumantam*) and great (*bṛhantam*): we kindle you (*samidhīmahi*), we make you blaze up, with fuel at the sacrifice (*adhvare*).

notes: ವಿಶ್ವವಾರಾ ಎಂಬ ಸ್ತ್ರೀಯು ದೇವತೆಯು; the bhāṣya calls her the ṛṣi
ಛಂದಃ ೧-೩. ತ್ರಿಷ್ಟುಪ್ and ೨. ಜಗತೀ overlap as printed

en: O Agni, of far-reaching wisdom, whose food is the oblation, endowed with radiance and of great nature, we make you blaze up at the sacrifice.
We kindle you at the sacrifice, wise Agni, whose food is the oblation , who are brilliant and vast.

notes: ಸೌಮಿ printed in the bhāṣya; ಸ್ತೌಮಿ?

en: O Agni, come (*ā gahi*) together with all (*viśvebhiḥ*) the gods, to the sacrificer who gives the oblations (*havyadātaye*), for his sake; come to the sacrifice. For we choose (*vṛṇīmahe*, "we pray to") you, the invoker (*hotāra*) of the gods.
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be gracious to come
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—who are the invoker of the gods
O Agni, we pray to you, the invoker of the gods, saying: be gracious to come, together with all the gods, to the sacrificer who offers the oblation.
Come, Agni, with all the gods, to the donor (of the oblation) : we have recourse to you as their invoker.

O Agni, bring (*ā vaha*, "cause to reach") fair strength (*suvīryam*) to the sacrificer (*yajamānāya*) who presses the Soma (*sunvate*). Further, sit down (*ā satsi*, "sit") together with the gods on the sacrificial grass (*barhiṣi*), that is, at the sacrifice.
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—cause to be obtained
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—on the seats of darbha grass
notes: ತ್ರ್ಯಯಮಾ in the bhāṣya, ತ್ರ್ಯರ್ಯಮಾ in the Anuvāda; the incipit is printed with a misprint?

en: O Agni, cause the sacrificer who presses the Soma juice to obtain excellent strength. Come with the gods and sit down on the seats of darbha grass.
To the institutor of the rite, pouring out the libation, bring excellent vigour ; sit down with the gods upon the sacred grass.

Sāyaṇa addresses Agni as "victor of a thousand" (the winner of a thousand), kindled with oblations and praiseworthy. As the messenger of the gods, he says, Agni nourishes our *dharmāṇi*, that is, our rites such as the sacrifice; *puṣyasi* means "you cause to thrive".
- सहस्रजित् (*sahasrajit*)—one who has won victory in thousands of situations
O Agni, who have won victory in thousands of situations, kindled with oblations and worthy of praise, you, as messenger of the gods, cause our sacrificial and other good rites to thrive.
Victor over thousands, you favour, when kindled, our holy rites, the honoured messenger of the gods.

Sāyaṇa addresses the sacrificers: "Establish Agni." He is *Jātavedas*, because he knows all beings that are born; the bearer of the *hotra*, that is, the carrier of the sacrifice; the youngest; the god, that is, the shining one; the *ṛtvij*, the one who sacrifices in the proper season. *Nidadhāta* means "establish".
- जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—him who knows all beings that have come into being
- होत्रवाहं (*hotravāhaṃ*)—who carries the oblations (to the gods)
- ऋत्विजं (*ṛtvijaṃ*)—who is the chief priest of the sacrifice

O sacrificers, establish and worship Agni, who knows all beings that have come into being, who carries the oblations to the gods, who is very youthful and shining, and who is the chief priest of the sacrifice.
Reverence Angi, by whom all that is, is known, the bearer of oblations the youngest of the gods, the divine, the ministrant priest.

Today, on this day, let the sacrifice, which is the means of sacrifice, namely the oblation, most pervaded by the shining praisers of the gods, go forth uninterrupted to the gods. O priests, spread the sacred grass for Agni's seat.
- देवव्यचस्तमः (*devavyacastamaḥ*)—offered with the utmost devotion by the shining praisers ⟨NOTE:62⟩
- प्र एतु (*pra etu*)—let it reach the gods (O priests)
notes: ಸೂಕ್ತ—೨೨ printed; the sūkta is ೨೯

en: In this sacrifice, let the oblation offered with the utmost devotion by the shining praisers duly reach the gods. O priests, spread the seat of darbha grass for Agni.
May the sacrifice most solemnly offered by the devout duly proceed to-day (to the gods) : spread the sacred grass for their seat.
The Maruts are the troops of Maruts; the Aśvins are the physicians of the gods; Mitra is the sun; and Varuṇa. All these gods, together with their entire retinue, are to sit down on this sacred grass.
- सर्वया विशा (*sarvayā viśā*)—with all the attendant gods belonging to them
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—upon these seats of darbha grass
May the Maruts, who are of divine nature, the Aśvin gods, Mitra and Varuṇa, together with all the attendant gods belonging to them, come and sit down upon these seats of darbha grass.
May the Maruts, the Ashwins, Mitra, Varuna, the gods, with all their attendants, sit down upon this grass.

Atri described the gift of the royal seers in the presence of Agni by means of this sūkta. O Vaiśvānara, leader of all men, Agni, you are *satpati*, the protector of the good and the righteous; *cetiṣṭha*, the most knowing; *asura*, the powerful; and *maghonaḥ*, one possessing wealth. Tryaruṇa, the royal seer of that name, son of Trivṛṣṇa, gave (*mamahe*) to me the two oxen *anasvantā* (that is, joined with a cart, *anas*) together with ten thousands of cattle, gold and the like. That royal seer is known (*ciketa*) to all people by this gift. ⟨NOTE:64⟩
notes: ತ್ರೀ ತ್ರೀಣ್ಯರ್ಯಮಾರ್ಯಮಾಣಿ: construction of the words uncertain

en: - दशभिः सहस्रैः (*daśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ*)—those joined with ten thousand pieces of gold
- चिकेत (*ciketa*)—he has become known and famous to all

O Agni, in the form of Vaiśvānara, protector of the good, best among the discerning, endowed with strength and wealth: the royal seer named Tryaruṇa, son of Trivṛṣṇa, gave me a pair of cattle (two oxen) joined with a cart and with ten thousand pieces of gold. For that very reason he has become known and famous to all.

Agni, who are the protector of the good, most wise, powerful, and opulent; Tryaruna, the son of Trivrishna, has become renowned, Vaishwanara, in that he has bestowed upon me a pair of cattle with a waggon, and with ten thousands of treasure.

Sāyaṇa explains that Tryaruṇa gives me hundreds of pieces of gold, twenty of cattle (*gonām* means *gavām*), and two horses (*harī*), which are yoked to a chariot and bear the yoke well (*sudhurā*). He then addresses Agni Vaiśvānara, well praised by us (*suṣṭuta*) ⟨NOTE:65⟩ and growing by the oblations (*vavṛdhāna*): bestow (*yaccha*, that is, *prayaccha*) happiness (*śarma*) on that Tryaruṇa.
notes: ಧೇನುಗಳಿರುವ ಪ್ರದೇಶಗಳನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸಿಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ: Sāyaṇa has ಗಾ = ಧೇನೂರ್ವೃಷ್ಟಿಲಕ್ಷಣಾನ್ಯುದಕಾನಿ, ಯಜಮಾನಂ ಗಾ ಲಂಭಯತಿ

en: - वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*)—who are of the form of Vaiśvānara
- ववृधानः (*vavṛdhānaḥ*)—and made to grow by oblations, you who are so
- शता च (*śatā ca*)—and a hundred pieces of gold
- सुधरा (*sudharā*)—those fit to bear a load
- त्रैरुणाय (*trairuṇāya*)—to the royal seer named Tryaruṇa

O Agni, who are of the form of Vaiśvānara, you who are well praised by us and made to grow by oblations: bring happiness to the royal seer named Tryaruṇa, who has given me a hundred pieces of gold, twenty cows, and two horses fit to bear a load and yoked to a chariot.
Agni, Vaishwanara, you are deservedly praised and exalted ( by us ); bestow happiness upon Tryaruna, who gives me hundreds (of Suvarnas), twenty cattle, and a pair of burden-bearing horses.

Tryaruṇa, hearing the many praises (*girah*) of me, who have many children (*tuvijāta*), is pleased; with a concentrated mind (*yuktena*, that is, *abhiyuktena*) he says to me again and again, "Take this, take this." In the same way, O Agni, who are exceedingly worthy of praise (*naviṣṭha*), Trasadasyu too, desiring a praise (*sumati*) that is newest (*navama*, that is, *navatama*) for you, has begged me, "Take this, take this."
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—(praising you), by the praises (being pleased)
- युक्तेन (*yuktena*)—with a mind full of devotion
- नविष्ठाय (*naviṣṭhāya*)—who are worthy of exceeding praise
- त्रसदस्युः (*trasadasyuḥ*)—Trasadasyu too (has begged me to accept these gifts)

O Agni, Tryaruṇa was gratified by the excellent praises composed and recited with you in view, so that your favour might be gained for Tryaruṇa; and he gave me, who have many sons, the most excellent gifts with devotion. In the same way Trasadasyu too, desiring that I compose an excellent praise with you in view for the gaining of your favour for himself, has begged me to accept excellent gifts.
As Tryaruna, pleased by the eulogies of me who have many children, presses with earnest (mind, gifts upon me), so does Trasadasvu. desirous, Agni, of your valued favour through your exceeding praise.

The petitioner who begs says to Aśvamedha, the royal seer, who is *sūri*, that is, the impeller and giver of wealth, "Give to me" (*pravocati*); that is, he begs wealth from Aśvamedha. Aśvamedha gives wealth (*sani*) to that petitioner who comes (*yate*) to him, that is, goes to his presence, with a *ṛc*, a praise of Agni. O Agni, give to that Aśvamedha, who desires the sacrifice (*ṛtāyate*), insight (*medhā*), that is, wisdom concerning the sacrifice.
- सूरये (*sūraye*)—who is a giver of wealth
- अश्वमेधाय (*aśvamedhāya*)—to the royal seer named Aśvamedha
- ऋचा (*ṛcā*)—together with a praise (that extols Agni)
- यते (*yate*)—to him who goes to him
- ऋतायते (*ṛtāyate*)—to that Aśvamedha, who desires the sacrifice

O Agni, the petitioner who approaches the royal seer named Aśvamedha, the giver of wealth, and begs wealth of him together with a praise that wins your favour and extols you, to such a man he gives wealth, in the faith that good will come to him from that praise. Give good understanding to that Aśvamedha, who desires the sacrifice.

When Ashwamedha gives to him who solicits of him as a benefactor, saying (bestow wealth) upon me, and comes (to him) with a verse (in your praise), do you, Agni, grant intelligence to (the Raja) who wishes to offer sacrifice (to you).

The hundred bulls (*ukṣaṇaḥ*, that is, oxen) given by Aśvamedha as gifts, which fulfil desires (*paruṣāḥ*), delight me exceedingly. O Agni, may those bulls, which have the three mixtures (*āśir*) of curds, barley meal and milk as the means of cooking ⟨NOTE:66⟩, be, like Soma, for your gratification.
notes: ಸಂವಿವ್ಯಾನಶ್ಚಿತ್: Kannada gloss ದೃಢಸಂಕಲ್ಪದಿಂದ ಸಂಚರಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವಾಗಲೇ differs from Sāyaṇa's ಸಂವೃಣ್ವಾನಃ ಸಂಗಚ್ಛಮಾನೋ ವೇಂದ್ರಃ

en: - त्रशिरः (*traśiraḥ*)—of the form of the three mixtures, curds and the rest
- उद्धर्षयंति (*uddharṣayaṃti*)—gratify (may they also serve for your gratification)

O Agni, just as the hundred bulls given by this same Aśvamedha, which fulfil desires, gratify me like Soma juices of the three mixtures of curds and the rest, so may the oblations given by him bring gratification to you.
Whose hundred robust oxen yield me delight, as the triple-mixed Soma, the offering of Ashwamedha (gratifies you).

O Indra and Agni, *śatadānni* means in him who gives to petitioners a hundred, that is, immeasurable, wealth (*śatadāvā*). In that Aśvamedha, the royal seer, establish (*dhārayatam*, that is, *nidhārayatam*) *kṣatra*, that is, wealth, endowed with good heroism (*suvīrya*), great and free from old age (*ajara*). How? As the sun in the sky (*divi*, that is, in the atmosphere).
- अश्वमेधे (*aśvamedhe*)—in the royal seer named Aśvamedha
- सूर‍्यं इव (*sūryaṃ iva*)—shining like the sun

O Indra and Agni, fill the royal seer named Aśvamedha, who gives wealth without measure, with wealth that is endowed with excellent strength, abundant, shining like the sun in the atmosphere, and everlasting.
Indra and Agni, bestow upon the munificent Ashwamedha infinite wealth with excellent posterity, undecaying as the sun in heaven.

Agni, fully kindled, spreads (*aśret*, that is, *śrayati*) his lustre in the shining atmosphere; likewise, facing the dawn, he shines widely (*urviyā*) and brilliantly. Viśvavārā, so named because she keeps off every sinful enemy, faces east (*prācī*, that is, *prāṅmukhī*); she praises the gods, Indra and the others, with praises (*namobhiḥ*), and, provided with oblations such as the *puroḍāśa* and with the ghee-ladle (*dhṛtācī*), goes towards Agni who is thus.
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods, Indra and the rest

Agni, fully kindled, spreads his lustre in the shining atmosphere. Facing the dawn, he shines widely. Praising Indra and the other gods with praises, and holding the ladle furnished with oblations, the seer named Viśvavārā goes towards Agni, facing him.

Agni, when kindled, spreads lustre through the firmament, and shines in widely the presence of the dawn: Vishwavara, facing the east, glorifying the gods with praises, and bearing the ladle with the oblation, proceeds (to the sacred fire).

O Agni, being well kindled, you rule (*rājasi*, that is, *īśiṣe*) over *amṛta*, that is, water. You also attend (*sacase*, that is, *sevase*) the sacrificer who makes oblations such as the *puroḍāśa*, for his welfare (*svastaye*), that is, for his freedom from destruction. Moreover, the sacrificer to whom you come (*invasi*, that is, *gacchasi*) holds all wealth (*dravinam*) of the kind that consists of cattle and the like. And, O Agni, he sets before you, as the guest that you are, the oblation fitting for your hospitality (*ātithya*).
- हविष्कृण्वंतं (*haviṣkṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- आतिथ्यं (*ātithyaṃ*)—the oblation fit for your worship as guest
- पुर इत् (*pura it*)—right in front of you

O Agni, when you are kindled you are lord of all the water. You attend the sacrificer who makes the oblation, so that welfare may come to him. The sacrificer whom you favour and attend obtains all wealth. O Agni, he places the oblation fit for your worship as guest right in front of you.

When about to be kindled, Agni, you rule over ambrosial (water) : you are present with the offerer of the oblation for his welfare: he to whom you repair acquires universal wealth ; he places before you, Agni, the dues of hospitality.

In the Pavitreṣṭi, the verse beginning *agne śardha* is the yājyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering. It is laid down in the sūtra: जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगायेति संयाज्ये (*juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāyeti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2. 12). In the Sākamedha offerings too, at the offering "to the sporting Maruts, a *puroḍāśa* on seven potsherds", the Sviṣṭakṛt yājyā is this same verse, and the sūtra says so: जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगायेति संयाज्ये (*juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāyeti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2. 18).

O Agni, for our great (*mahate*, that is, abundant) good fortune (*saubhaga*, that is, good wealth), *śardha*: overcome the enemies. Let your *dyumnāni*, that is, riches or splendours, be excellent. Moreover, O Agni, make *jāspatya* (*jā* is wife, and the husband too; the pair is *jāyāpatī*) well-regulated, that is, closely joined to one another; make it good. And overcome (*abhi tiṣṭha*, that is, attack) the energies of the rivals who wish for themselves an enemy.
- सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*)—so that blessed wealth may come to us
- जास्पत्यं (*jāspatyaṃ*)—the good rites that point to the mutual relation of husband and wife
- सुयमं (*suyamaṃ*)—joined to one another, as if under one rule
- शत्रूयतां (*śatrūyatāṃ*)—of those who wish us harm
- अभि तिष्ठ (*abhi tiṣṭha*)—check and stand against

O Agni, check our enemies, so that blessed wealth may come to us in abundance. Let your riches be excellent. Perfect the good rites that point to the mutual relation of husband and wife, joined to one another as if under one rule. Check and overcome the energies of those who wish us harm.
Repress, Agni, (our foes to ensure our) exceeding prosperity : may your riches ever be excellent : preserve in concord the relation of man and wife, and overpower the energies of the hostile.

In the Pavitreṣṭi, this verse beginning अग्ने शर्ध (*agne śardha*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra at the Sviṣṭakṛt offering; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगायेति संयाज्ये (*juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāyeti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-12). Again, in the Sākamedha sacrifices, when the offering is made with the words मरुद्भ्यः क्रीडिभ्यः पुरोडाशं सप्तकपालं (*marudbhyaḥ krīḍibhyaḥ puroḍāśaṃ saptakapālaṃ*), this verse is to be recited as the yājyā mantra at the Sviṣṭakṛt offering; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगायेति संयाज्ये (*juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāyeti saṃyājye*) (Ā. 2-18).

O Agni, I, the sacrificer, praise (*stauti*) ⟨NOTE:69⟩ the glory (*śrī*), that is, the brightness, that belongs to you, who are kindled, that is, grown strong, of excellent splendour (*pramahas*). You are the showerer (*vṛṣabha*) of desires and are wealthy (*dyumnavān*). In the sacrifices (*adhvareṣu*) you are well kindled.
notes: ಸ್ವಶ್ವಪುತ್ರೇಣ ಸೂರ್ಯೇಣ: reading doubtful

en: - प्र महसः (*pra mahasaḥ*)—and who have most excellent splendour
- सं इध्यसे (*saṃ idhyase*)—you are well kindled
O Agni, I bow to the splendour of you, who are fully kindled and have most excellent splendour. You, the showerer of desires, are wealthy with brightness. In the sacrifices you are well kindled.
I praise the glory, Agni, of you when kindled and blazing fiercely : you are the affluent showerer ( of benefits ), you are fitly lighted at sacrifices.

In the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices, the two verses beginning *samiddho agna āhuta* are the two Sāmidhenī verses. The sūtra says so: समिद्धो अग्न आहुतेति द्वे (*samiddho agna āhuteti dve*) (Ā. 1-2). O invoked one (*āhuta*), called from every side by the sacrificers; O one of good sacrifice (*svadhvara*); O Agni, being fully kindled, worship (*yakṣi*, that is, *yajasva*) the gods, Indra and the other shining ones. For you are the bearer of the oblations (*havyavāṭ*, that is, *havyānāṃ voḍhā*); for that reason, the connection is, worship the gods.

O Agni, called by the sacrificers and having an excellent sacrifice, you are the bearer of the oblation to the gods. Therefore, as soon as you are kindled by the sacrificer, perform the sacrifice for the gods.
Agni, you are kindled and invoked ; worship the gods at the holy rite, for you are the bearer of the oblation.

In the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices, this Ṛk beginning समिद्दो अग्न आहुत (*samiddo agna āhuta*) and the following Ṛk are to be used as sāmidhenī mantras; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, समिद्दो अग्न आहुतेति द्वे (*samiddo agna āhuteti dve*) (Ā. Sū. 1-2).

O priests, when our sacrifice has begun, make offering to Agni, the bearer of the oblations (हव्यवाहनं (*havyavāhanaṃ*)), from every side; likewise serve him, and choose him. That Agni who is named Havyavāhana is connected with the gods, and that he is to be chosen by the sacrificers, is stated plainly in the Taittirīya (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-8-6): there are three Agnis, Havyavāhana of the gods, Kavyavāhana of the fathers, and Sahaṃrakṣas of the Asuras. These now hope, "he will choose me, me"; by saying "choose Havyavāhana" he chooses the one who belongs to the gods.
- प्रयति (*prayati*)—as soon as it has begun
- वृणीध्वं (*vṛṇīdhvaṃ*)—choose (him as the messenger who brings your oblation to the gods)
O priests, as soon as our sacrifice has begun, offer the oblation to Agni, who carries the oblation. Worship him and choose him as the messenger who brings your oblation to the gods.
Offer worship and adoration to Agni, when the sacrifice is solemnized ; select the bearer of the oblation to the gods.

In the sacrifice that belongs to Manu there are three splendours (त्री त्रीण्यर्यमार्यमाणि (*trī trīṇyaryamāryamāṇi*)) ⟨NOTE:73⟩; and the Maruts uphold three shining lights, divine and in the atmosphere, which have the nature of wind, fire and sun, those splendours. The Maruts, of pure strength, praise you, Indra; you, wise one, are the seer of these Maruts, that is, you become their seer.
notes: ಶುಷ್ಕಮೇತನ್ನಾಮಕಮಸುರಂ in the bhāṣya, but ಶುಷ್ಣಂ in the Ṛk and the gloss

en: - त्री रोचना (*trī rocanā*)—three masses of splendour

In the sacrifice that belongs to Manu and is meant for worshipping the gods, three splendours are established. The Maruts uphold three masses of splendour, which are in the atmosphere and have the forms of fire, wind and sun. O Indra, the Maruts, whose strength is pure, worship you. You are the wise seer of those Maruts.

In the adoration of the gods by Manu there are three effulgences, and they, (the Maruts), uphold three luminaries in heaven : the Maruts of pure energy worship you, for you, Indra, are their intelligent Rishi.

When the Maruts praised Indra, who was delighted, having drunk the pressed Soma, then Indra took up the thunderbolt. Then, when he slew Ahi, that is Vṛtra, he let the mighty waters, which Vṛtra had held back, go forth to flow freely, and freed them from their confinement.
- अनु आर्चन् (*anu ārcan*)—praised with devotion, then (Indra)

As soon as the Maruts praised with devotion Indra, who had drunk the pressed Soma and was satisfied, Indra took the thunderbolt in his hand. As soon as Indra destroyed the Asura Vṛtra, he released the abundant waters to flow freely.
When the Maruts worship Indra, exulting and drinking of the effused libation, he grasps the thunderbolt wherewith he destroys Ahi, and sets the abundant waters free to flow.

O Maruts, mighty ones, you and Indra drink this Soma of mine, well pressed; the genitive stands in the sense of the accusative. The oblation drunk by you, consisting of Soma, makes the sacrificer find cows, that is, the waters that take the form of rain; it makes the sacrificer obtain cows. Moreover Indra, having drunk this Soma, slew Ahi, that is Vṛtra.
- तद्धि हव्यं (*taddhi havyaṃ*)—that same oblation, drunk by you
- मनुषे (*manuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice

O Maruts, mighty in form, you and Indra drink this well-pressed Soma juice. That same oblation, drunk by you, makes known to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice the regions where the cows are. Indra, having drunk this Soma, destroyed Vṛtra. ⟨NOTE:74⟩
notes: ಹಿಂಸಿತವಾಗಿಂದ್ರಿಯಾನ್ in the bhāṣya; the Kannada gloss has ಹಿಂಸಾತ್ಮಕವಾದ ವಾಕ್ಕುಳ್ಳ

en: Or, mighty Maruts, and you also, Indra, drink of this my copiously-effused libation : then the offered libation obtains cattle for the offerer, and Indra, drinking of it, kills Ahi.

Indra, endowed with supreme lordship, after drinking the Soma made the two worlds, heaven and earth, most firm; he made them unmoving. Enveloping (or: coming together, or going; Sāyaṇa derives the word from a root meaning to cover or from one meaning to go) ⟨NOTE:75⟩, he made Vṛtra, who fled like a deer, afraid. Indra, freeing from his covering the Dānava, son of Danu, namely Vṛtra, who was concealing himself, panting to cause fear, advanced against him and slew him.
notes: number of the Ṛk not printed after the Pada; read as 12 from the sequence

en: - आत् (*āt*)—as soon as the Soma was drunk
- संविव्यानश्चित् (*saṃvivyānaścit*)—while moving about with firm resolve
- मृगं (*mṛgaṃ*)—Vṛtra, who was fleeing like a deer
- भियसे कः (*bhiyase kaḥ*)—made him be overcome with fear
- श्वसंतं (*śvasaṃtaṃ*)—who was breathing in a hideous way so that others should fear

The lord Indra, as soon as the Soma was drunk, established heaven and earth exceedingly and firmly. While he was moving about with firm resolve to destroy his enemy, he made Vṛtra, who was fleeing like a deer, be overcome with fear. He prevented Vṛtra, the son of Danu, who tried to cover himself and was breathing hideously so that others should fear, from hiding, confronted him and destroyed him.

Thereupon he fixed firmly heaven and earth, and, resolutely advancing filled (Vritra), like a deer, with terror : stripping off his covering, Indra slew the Danava, endeavouring to hide, and panting with affright.

And further, O Maghavan, O wealthy Indra, through your own deed all the shining gods, Agni and the others, have granted you in due order the drinking of Soma for your sake; from then on Indra became greater than all the gods. So it is heard: स महान्भात्वा देवता अब्रवीदुद्धारं म उद्धरतेत्यादि । (*sa mahānbhātvā devatā abravīduddhāraṃ ma uddharatetyādi |*) (Ai. Brā. 3-21) ⟨NOTE:76⟩. Since you, O Indra, made the tawny horses of Sūrya, which were coming on and were in front, slow of pace for the sake of the seer named Etaśa ⟨NOTE:77⟩, that is, Etaśa had competed with Sūrya, the son of his own horse ⟨NOTE:78⟩; and another passage says the same: प्रैतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानं सौवश्यॆ सुष्टिमावदिंद्रः (*praitaśaṃ sūrye paspṛdhānaṃ sauvaśyè suṣṭimāvadiṃdraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-15) ⟨NOTE:79⟩.
notes: ಗವ್ಯಂಚಿತ್ ಗೋಸಂಬಂಧಿ…ನಮಷ್ಯಪೂರ್ವಂ ಸಮೂಹಂ: letters damaged

en: - एतशे (*etaśe*)—(O Indra) for the help of the seer named Etaśa
- पुरः सतीः (*puraḥ satīḥ*)—that were spreading out in front
- उपराः कः (*uparāḥ kaḥ*)—you made slow of pace
- अनु आदुदुः (*anu āduduḥ*)—approved (to you first, before all others)

O Indra, by that greatness of yours by which, for the help of the seer named Etaśa, you made the horses that belong to Sūrya, which were coming against you and spreading out in front, slow of pace, for that very reason all the gods, pleased by your surpassing deed, approved the drinking of Soma for you, O wealthy Indra, before all others.
Then, for this exploit, all the gods gave you, Maghavan, in succession, the Soma beverage ; whence you have retarded, for the sake of Etasa, the advancing horses of the sun.

When the wealthy Indra split with his thunderbolt at one stroke the nine and ninety strongholds of Śambara (the word अस्य (*asya*) here denotes Śambara; भोगान् (*bhogān*) means cities), then the Maruts, in the place of their common abode, that is, in the battle, praised Indra who stood there, with a hymn in the Triṣṭubh metre. Thus praised, Indra oppressed the shining Asura named Śambara by the mantra employed by the Maruts; the verb बाधत (*bādhata*) means he crushed.
- नव नवतिं च (*nava navatiṃ ca*)—ninety-nine in number

As soon as the wealthy Indra split asunder at one time, with his thunderbolt, the ninety-nine cities of Śambara, the Maruts worshipped Indra, who stood in one place, with praises composed in the Triṣṭubh metre. Indra, pleased by the recitation of these very mantras, harmed the shining Śambara.

Whereupon Maghavan has destroyed with his thunderbolt at once his (Shambara's) ninety and nine cities: the Maruts glorifying Indra in a common dwelling with the Trishtubh hymn, he destroyed the bright (city of the Asura).

Agni, the friend of Indra, quickly cooked three hundred buffaloes, that is, animals, for the friend, this Indra, by a deed that served as the cause. And Indra, endowed with supreme lordship, drank at one time, for the slaying of Vṛtra, the pressed Soma that stood in the three सरांसि (*sarāṃsi*) of Manu, that is, vessels; here the word सरः (*saraḥ*) is said to stand for the vessels named Pūtabhṛt, Ādhavanīya and Droṇakalaśa ⟨NOTE:80⟩.
- त्रि शतानि (*tri śatāni*)—three hundred in number
- महिषा (*mahiṣā*)—animals in the form of buffaloes
- त्रि सरांसि (*tri sarāṃsi*)—that is in three Droṇakalaśa vessels
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—that was pressed according to the rule
- वृत्रहत्याय (*vṛtrahatyāya*)—to gain strength to kill Vṛtra

Agni, the friend of Indra, cooked three hundred animals in the form of buffaloes to help his dear friend Indra in his enemy-destroying deed. Indra drank at one time the Soma juice offered by Manu, which was in three Droṇakalaśa vessels and had been pressed according to the rule, and gained the strength needed for the slaying of Vṛtra.

To aid (the undertaking of) his friend, Agni, the friend (of Indra), has quickly consumed three hundred buffaloes ; and Indra, for the destruct- ion of Vritra, has at once quaffed three vessels of Sama, offered by Manu. ⟨NOTE:81⟩

O Indra, when you ate the flesh of three hundred buffaloes, that is, animals (the verb अघः (*aghaḥ*) stands for eating), and when you, the wealthy one, drank three vessels made of Soma, and when Indra slew Ahi, that is Vṛtra, then all the gods summoned Indra for battle, since he was filled by the drinking of Soma and the like. The example is कारं न (*kāraṃ na*): as a master calls his servant.
- त्री शता (*trī śatā*)—three hundred in number
- कारं न (*kāraṃ na*)—as masters call a servant

O Indra, when you ate the flesh of three hundred animals in the form of buffaloes, when you, the wealthy one, drank all the Soma that filled the three Droṇakalaśa vessels, and when you, Indra, slew Vṛtra, then all the gods summoned Indra, who was filled by the drinking of Soma, for battle, as masters call a servant.

When you have eaten the flesh of the three hundred buffaloes, when you who are Maghavan have drunk the three vessels of Soma, and had slain Ahi. then all the gods summoned Indra, full of food, as if he had been a servant, to the battle.

The Ṛk उशना यत्सहस्यै (*uśanā yatsahasyai*) belongs to the Stoma of Uśanas, and in the Marutvatīya rite it is the opening verse of the sūkta. The sūtra says: उशनसः स्तोमेन गरगीर्णमिवात्मानं मन्यमानो यजेतोशना यत्सहस्यैरयातं । (*uśanasaḥ stomena garagīrṇamivātmānaṃ manyamāno yajetośanā yatsahasyairayātaṃ |*) (Ā. Sū. 9-5): one who thinks of himself as if he had swallowed poison should sacrifice with the Stoma of Uśanas. Sāyaṇa explains: when you, O Indra, and Uśanā Kāvya went to the house of Kutsa with swift horses that overcome their foes, then, O Indra, at that time you went, slaying your enemies, in one and the same chariot with Kutsa and the gods; and you also slew the Asura named Śuṣka ⟨NOTE:82⟩.
- सहस्यैः (*sahasyaiḥ*)—that have the power to resist enemies

O Indra, when you and Uśanas, joining together, went to the house of Kutsa with horses that have the power to resist enemies and are swift, you went, destroying your enemies, seated in one chariot with Kutsa and the other gods. And you also harmed the Asura named Śuṣṇa.

When, Indra, you and Ushanas, with vigorous and rapid coursers went to the dwelling of Kutsa, then, destroying his foes, you went in one chariot with Kutsa and the gods, and verily you have slain Sushna.

When the Stoma of Uśanas is recited, this ninth Ṛk of the sūkta, उशना यत्सहस्यैः (*uśanā yatsahasyaiḥ*), is to be recited as the first Ṛk among the Marutvatīya śastra mantras; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, उशनसस्तोमेन गरगीर्णमिवात्मानं मन्यमानो यजेतोशना यत्सहस्यैरयातं (*uśanasastomena garagīrṇamivātmānaṃ manyamāno yajetośanā yatsahasyairayātaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 9-5).

O Indra, of the two-wheeled chariot of Sūrya you formerly took away one wheel and set it apart; the other wheel you made over to Kutsa, that he might attain wealth (वरिवः (*varivaḥ*) is wealth). Further, the Dasyus, the Asuras, are अनासः (*anāsaḥ*), without a mouth; by the word for mouth, sound is meant, so they are soundless and dumb. These you killed with your weapon, the thunderbolt. In the battle (दुर्योणे (*duryoṇe*)) you utterly split the Asuras whose organ of speech is harmed ⟨NOTE:83⟩. The doubling of the verbs अमृणः (*amṛṇaḥ*) and न्यवृणगिति (*nyavṛṇagiti*) is for emphasis.
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—(O Indra,) of Sūrya (of the chariot with two wheels)
- अनासः (*anāsaḥ*)—who were without a mouth and dumb
- वधेन (*vadhena*)—with the thunderbolt, the means of killing
- मृध्रवाचः (*mṛdhravācaḥ*)—the Asuras whose speech is harmful
- नि अवृणक् (*ni avṛṇak*)—you have cut through completely

O Indra, of the two wheels of Sūrya's chariot you set one apart; the other you made a help to Kutsa for obtaining wealth. With the thunderbolt, the means of killing, you harmed the Asuras who were without a mouth and dumb. In battle you have cut through completely the Asuras whose speech is harmful.

You have formerly detached one wheel (of the car) of Surya : another you have given to Kutsa wherwith to acquire wealth : with the thunderbolt you have confounded the voiceless Dasyus, you have destroyed in battle the speech-bereft (foes).
O Indra, the praises that belong to me, the seer named Gauriviti, increase you; let them make you grow. You brought the Asura named Pipru under the power of Ṛjiśvan, the son of Vidathin.

O Indra, a certain seer named Ṛjiśvan, for the sake of your friendship, cooking the offerings fit for cooking, the cakes (puroḍāśa) and the like, has turned you towards himself. And you drank the Soma of this Ṛjiśvan.
- गौरिवीतेः (*gaurivīteḥ*)—(O Indra,) made by me, who am named Gauriviti
- वैदथिनाय (*vaidathināya*)—for Ṛjiśvan, the son of Vidathi
- पक्तिः (*paktiḥ*)—the cakes and the like that are fit for cooking
- आ चक्रे (*ā cakre*)—has turned towards himself

O Indra, may the praises made by me, who am named Gauriviti, make you grow. For Ṛjiśvan, the son of Vidathi, you brought the Asura named Pipu under his power. That same Ṛjiśvan, to win your friendship, cooking the cakes and the like that are fit for cooking, has turned you towards himself. Drink his Soma.

May the praises of Gauriviti exalt you ; you have humbled Pipru for the son of Vidathin : Rijishwan preparing dressed viands, has, through your friendship, brought you (to his presence), and you have drunk of his libation.

On the day of the Daśapeya, in the Marutvatīya śastra, the Ṛk नवग्वासः (*navagvāsaḥ*) is the sūktamukhīya, the opening verse of the sūkta. The sūtra says so: नवग्वासः सुतसोमास इंद्रं सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवग्वैरिति निविद्वानयोराद्ये । (*navagvāsaḥ sutasomāsa iṃdraṃ sakhā ha yatra sakhibhirnavagvairiti nividvānayorādye |*) (Ā. Sū. 9-3). Those who perform a sattra sacrifice and go home having completed it in nine months are the navagvas; those who go having completed it in ten months are the daśagvas. These two kinds of Aṅgirases, having pressed the Soma, worship Indra with arkas, that is, with hymns fit for worship; they praise him. Likewise the praising leaders, the Aṅgirases, opened up the herd of cattle, well known in many places, which Vala the Asura had covered ⟨NOTE:85⟩.
- नवग्वासः (*navagvāsaḥ*)—those who complete the sacrifice in nine months
- दशग्वासः (*daśagvāsaḥ*)—the sons of Aṅgiras who complete it in ten months
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the Aṅgirases, who are also leaders
- ऊर्वं (*ūrvaṃ*)—in the form of a mass
- गव्यं चित् (*gavyaṃ cit*)—that was filled with cattle
- अप व्रन् (*apa vran*)—became able to open

The sons of Aṅgiras, known as navagvas and daśagvas, ready to press the Soma juice and offer it to Indra, worship him with praises. The Aṅgirases, who praise Indra and are his leaders, became able to open the cave that was filled with a mass of cattle and covered by Vala.

The observers of the nine month's celebration, those of the ten months, pouring out libations, worship Indra with hymns : the leaders (of rites), glorifying him have set open the cave (concealing the cattle).

At the time of the Soma-drinking of the sacrifice called Daśapeya, when the Marutvatīya śastra mantras are recited, this Ṛk नवग्वासः (*navagvāsaḥ*) is to be recited as the opening Ṛk of the sūkta; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the aphorism
नवग्वासः सुतसोमास इंद्रं सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवगैरिति निविद्दानयोराद्ये (*navagvāsaḥ sutasomāsa iṃdraṃ sakhā ha yatra sakhibhirnavagairiti nividdānayorādye*) (Ā. Sū. 9-3).

Among the Aṅgirasa seers it is the custom to call those who finish a sattra sacrifice and attain success in nine months navagva, and those who finish it in ten months daśagva. We have already explained the meaning of the words navagva and daśagva in Ṛ. Saṃ., Part 6, p. 24.

In the one-day rite called Parikrī, in the Marutvatīya and the Niṣkevalya, the first two Ṛks, कथो नु त (*katho nu ta*), are the sūktamukhīya. The sūtra says so: कथो नु ते परि चराणि विद्वानिति द्वे (*katho nu te pari carāṇi vidvāniti dve*) (Ā. Sū. 9-5). O wealthy Indra, knowing those heroic deeds which you have done, how shall I serve you, that is, perform service to you? O strongest Indra, whatever new heroic deeds you quickly do, those deeds of yours we shall proclaim at the sacrifices.
- परि चराणि (*pari carāṇi*)—can I offer worship
- शविष्ठ (*śaviṣṭha*)—O Indra, endowed with the greatest strength
- प्रेदु ब्रवाम (*predu bravāma*)—we praise and proclaim

O wealthy Indra, knowing fully the nature of the heroic deeds that you have accomplished, in what way can I offer worship to you? O Indra, endowed with the greatest strength, whichever new heroic deeds you do, all those heroic deeds of yours I shall praise and proclaim at the sacrifices.

Although, knowing the heroic acts which, Maghavan, you ahve performed, how may I adequately offer you adoration ? most mighty Indra, we ever celebrate at sacred rites the recent exploits which you have achieved.

In the one-day rite called Parikrī, in the Marutvatīya and Niṣkevalya śastra mantras, this Ṛk कथो नु ते (*katho nu te*) and the next Ṛk are to be recited as the opening mantras; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, कथो नु ते परि चराणि विद्वानिति द्वे (*katho nu te pari carāṇi vidvāniti dve*) (Ā. Sū. 9-5).

O Indra, unencompassed by your foes, by your innate strength you have made all these many things, which are perceived plainly, all that is pervasive and born in the worlds. O wielder of the thunderbolt, Indra, who bring your rivals low, whatever you quickly do, there is no one at all who can check that strength of yours.
- वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)—O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt
- तस्याः तविष्याः (*tasyāḥ taviṣyāḥ*)—to that very power

O Indra, without anyone's opposition, by your innate strength alone you have made the whole universe, abundant and plainly perceived by all. O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt, you who destroy your enemies, whatever deeds you quickly do, there is no one who can obstruct that very power of yours.

Unmatched (by any), you have done, Indra, all these many ( deeds ) by your innate energy : wielder of the thunderbolt, whatever you, the humbler of (foes), have undertaken, there is no one the arrester of this your prowess.
